What is Zika:
Zika is a flavivirus from the Flaviviridae family, which was first isolated in 1947 in a Rhesus monkey during an epidemiological study for yellow fever in the Zika forest in Uganda, Africa.
Twenty years later, the Zika virus was isolated in humans in Nigeria, and since then, it has spread to various regions of Africa and Asia, and has also reached Oceania.
The first case of the Zika virus in Brazil was discovered in 2015. It is believed that the virus arrived in the country via tourists who visited Brazil during the 2014 World Cup.
Zika is transmitted by Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus, and other Aedes species mosquitoes. After an incubation period of approximately 4 days, the first signs and symptoms appear.
The disease caused by the Zika virus is self-limiting and usually benign, characterized by fever, conjunctivitis, photophobia, joint pain, and rashes, which usually last from 2 to 7 days. However, only 18% of infected people have symptoms, and there are no fatalities.
Although the symptoms are similar to those of Dengue and Chikungunya, the condition is milder and resembles an allergy. There is no vaccine against the Zika virus, so treatment is aimed only at relieving symptoms.

The holes where water disappears into the ground are called sinkholes, swallow holes, or disappearing points.
In contrast to sinkholes, springs are places where water emerges. Slovenia is full of them – they differ in their mode of operation and the amount of water they produce. Spouting springs are springs where huge amounts of water emerge. There are also springs where water barely trickles. Thermal and mineral springs are rare in Slovenia and are characteristic of its eastern part.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Taking a break from running is just as important as a long run. Rest strengthens the body, improves focus, and increases motivation to run.

Your muscles recover more easily:
When you run, microscopic tears occur in the muscle fibers, and the body responds by trying to strengthen the muscles. However, this response only occurs if the body has time to do so. Depending on the length and intensity of the workout, the body needs at least 36-48 hours to recover. If it doesn’t get this time, it has no chance to recover and strengthen, but only to break down. This can lead to injuries, and your plans can quickly fall apart.

You avoid stress fractures:
If you want to avoid unpleasant injuries, rest is essential. Running is good for your bones, but the impact of running is strenuous for both the tissue and the muscles, which forces the bone to strengthen. However, if you run every day, neither the tissue, the muscles, nor the bones have time to strengthen properly. This can consequently lead to stress fractures.

Tendons are protected:
Tendons are connective tissue that attach muscles to bones, so they are constantly under stress when the body moves. Unfortunately, blood doesn’t reach them easily, so they need more time to recover than tissue where blood flow is greater. If they don’t get this time, chronic injuries can occur, such as tendinitis, which is inflammation caused by overuse or, in this case, activity.

Your brain can relax:
Running is a great way to relax, but at the same time, the stress hormone cortisol is released in the body during running. The body doesn’t know whether you’re running away from danger or for fun. Unfortunately, this elevated cortisol causes mood changes, irritability, sleep problems, and other health issues. That’s why it’s important to have rest days so that your body and well-being are in balance.

We can impose constant prohibitions and commands on a child with the intention of protecting them from negative experiences. Constant prohibitions can lead to rebellion or a lack of independence. A child who is naturally strong-willed may rebel and remain a perpetual rebel even as an adult. Alternatively, we can raise a child who always expects others to lead and guide them. This often results in a more compliant child who, even as an adult, is unable to make independent decisions.
However, it is best to raise a child into an independent individual who, as they grow up, is capable of making decisions about their own life. Even as a child, they need experiences from which they can learn. These experiences lead to internal discipline. Experiences and internal discipline help them to make the right decisions, decisions they make for themselves, not because of external circumstances.
Using prohibitions or commands:
We forbid a child from doing something or demand that they do something; this is a final decision without explanation, and the child must do it. This is our decision, and we do not consider the child's perspective.
Setting boundaries:
We inform the child that something is necessary for certain reasons. We explain what we want and are also open to their desires. We coordinate interests. The boundaries we set and that are accepted by everyone in the family gradually become rules. We consider the child's perspective.
When we set boundaries for a child, it is important to have a good reason. When it comes to their safety or morality, we also explain why they cannot or must do something. When we explain the reasons to the child, we are having a conversation with them, and they also have the opportunity to express their opinion. When a child expresses their opinion, they are thinking about the situation. In the conversation, we consider the child's age.
When we want to limit something, we can say that they can do it later, allow them to do something, and set a boundary. We show the situation to the child by talking about what they are allowed to do, not about what is forbidden. For example: "Because you are very hungry, I will allow you to eat one cookie before lunch."
Two-year-old children like to climb. A child climbs from a chair onto a table in the kitchen. We take them off the table and firmly say that this is not allowed. We tell them that we eat at the table. They can climb on the climbing frame at the playground.
Boundaries give a child a sense of security and reliability. It is good to be consistent with boundaries. The child may try to cross the boundaries, but we must be firm in our decisions. Firmness tells the child that we are serious. When a child knows what is allowed and what is not, they feel safe. Gradually, the child accepts these boundaries, and they become rules in the family. A rule in the family could be: "We brush our teeth before bed."
When we are not sure how to decide, we tell the child that we need to think about it and discuss it because then we get an overview of the situation and can make a decision more easily. The child realizes that we are considering them.
We can negotiate with an older child.
Example:
The child wants to stay at a friend's house for two hours, we would let them stay for half an hour, so we agree on one hour.
Sometimes we need to talk to our partner. We tell the child this.
Fear of problems often leads us to make wrong decisions because fear is not a healthy emotion. Love, consideration for all family members, and conversations within the family allow us to have good relationships and a happy upbringing.

A calorie is a unit of measurement that, technically speaking, defines the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of water by 1 °C at a pressure of 1 atmosphere.
Therefore, calories are not components of food, but rather a measure of the amount of energy (heat) we obtain from food. One (1) dietary calorie contains 4,184 joules of energy, and as such, a calorie is simply a calorie.
However, when it comes to the human body, things are no longer so simple.
Our body is an extremely complex biochemical system with programmed processes to regulate energy balance. The foods we consume go through various processes and trigger different effects, including on hormones and brain centers that control hunger and eating behavior.
The amount of energy in a particular food depends, of course, on its chemical composition.
As mentioned in Chapter 7, we obtain 9 kcal from 1 gram of fat, which is almost twice as much energy as we obtain from 1 gram of carbohydrates or protein. The amount of energy an individual actually needs depends primarily on their metabolism and exposure to exertion and stress.
However, the belief that all calories are equally problematic is one of the biggest misconceptions about healthy eating.
If we eat 100 calories of candy, it will have a different effect on our body than 100 calories of cauliflower. For example, if we want to lose weight sustainably, we need to avoid foods that provide a lot of calories but don't make us feel full, and replace them with foods that fill us up without being high in calories, such as vegetables.
The average daily energy intake, calculated in calories, is approximately 2500 kcal for men and approximately 2000 kcal for women. Foods are basically low-calorie and high-calorie. Food that has up to 40 kcal per serving is low-calorie, and a drink that has up to 20 kcal/100 ml is also low-calorie.
We can read the calorie content of foods with sufficient accuracy on the packaging of purchased food products and in calorie tables. However, for healthy eating that provides an appropriate balance of health and well-being, as well as an appropriate body weight, more is needed than just accurately counting calories. Not all calories are the same.
Let's compare different foods in terms of energy and calories.
Let's look at some illustrative examples. A handful of nuts contains approximately 175 calories, the same as a chocolate cookie. New research shows that nuts have quality calories, which puts them among good foods, while cookies are not.
Avocado contains many beneficial nutrients, but also relatively many calories, especially compared to other fresh fruits and vegetables. However, avocado calories are still considered to be of high quality.
Low-calorie beer, on the other hand, does not have a high nutritional value. It is also very important to be aware of the importance of "empty" calories – that is, foods that provide a lot of energy but little nutritional value.
Let's look at a lollipop as an illustrative example, which you always see in stores near the cash registers so that your little ones don't miss them. It has approximately 45 kcal, which is only slightly more than an apple. However, can we even compare the nutritional value of these two foods? Absolutely not! Because of the former, your little ones will, at best, visit the dentist very often because of cavities.
Therefore, don't just count calories, but choose them carefully.

Carbon–hydrogen bond -- The carbon-hydrogen bond (C--H bond) is a bond between carbon and hydrogen atoms that can be found in many organic compounds. This bond is a covalent bond meaning that carbon shares its outer valence electrons with up to four hydrogens. This completes both of their outer shells making them stable. Carbon--hydrogen bonds have a bond length of about 1.09 Å (1.09 × 10 m) and a bond energy of about 413 kJ/mol (see table below). Using Pauling's scale--C (2.55) and H (2.2)--the electronegativity difference between these two atoms is 0.35. Because of this small difference in electronegativities, the C−H bond is generally regarded as being non-polar. In structural formulas of molecules, the hydrogen atoms are often omitted. Compound classes consisting solely of C--H bonds and C--C bonds are alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic hydrocarbons. Collectively they are known as hydrocarbons.

The kitchen is often called the heart of the home. It's where we gather and prepare food that keeps us healthy and well-nourished. However, just like in other areas of your home, the kitchen can harbor hidden dangers that can make you sick. Some can cause digestive upset within a few days, while others can be fatal, especially for young children and those with weakened immune systems. If you're feeling under the weather, it might be time to take a closer look at your kitchen and make some changes.

Improper Food Handling
One of the biggest health hazards in your kitchen is you and how you handle food. If food isn't cooked and handled safely, bacteria can multiply rapidly, leading to foodborne illnesses that range from a few hours of digestive upset to death.

Are you guilty of any of these mistakes?
- Undercooking food: Food needs to be cooked to a safe internal temperature to kill bacteria. Undercooked meat, poultry, fish, or raw cookie dough are especially dangerous for young children or anyone with a weakened immune system.
- Leaving leftovers at room temperature for too long: Leaving food at room temperature allows bacteria to grow rapidly. Hot foods should be kept above 140 degrees F, and cold foods should be kept below 40 degrees F. This includes foods that are being thawed or marinated. Never leave food at room temperature for more than two hours. Thaw food slowly in the refrigerator or quickly in the microwave, and use it immediately.
- Not washing produce: All fresh produce should be washed before eating or using in cooking to remove dirt, bacteria, and pesticides.
- Rinsing raw meat: You should never rinse raw meat before cooking. Rinsing raw meat in the sink can spread bacteria to other surfaces in your kitchen. Cooking meat to a safe internal temperature will kill any harmful bacteria.
- Cross-contamination: Never use the same cutting board or utensils for raw and cooked food. Store raw meat on the bottom shelf of the refrigerator to prevent it from dripping onto other foods.
- Not washing your hands: Wash your hands frequently while cooking, especially after handling raw meat, poultry, or eggs.

Spoiled Food
Almost everyone has some food in their refrigerator or pantry that is past its expiration date. Eating or cooking with food that is past its prime can be dangerous. When in doubt, throw it out! Don't taste it to see if it's still good. The bacteria that can cause food poisoning can't be seen, smelled, or tasted.

Preventing food poisoning starts at the grocery store. Choose fruits and vegetables that are firm and free of bruises or insect damage. Avoid canned goods that are bulging, dented, or rusty. Packaged foods should be sealed tightly and free of leaks.

Kitchen Towels
Kitchen towels are a staple in most kitchens and a great way to reduce paper towel use. However, they can also be a breeding ground for bacteria if they're not washed frequently. According to a study by the National Sanitation Foundation International, 75% of kitchen towels tested positive for bacteria, including coliform bacteria, which can cause food poisoning.

Use separate towels for cleaning, food preparation, and hand drying. Wash kitchen towels frequently in hot water with bleach.

Can Openers
Whether you use a manual or electric can opener, the blade comes into contact with the contents of the can. This can lead to cross-contamination and the spread of bacteria.

Wash manual can openers in hot, soapy water after each use. For electric can openers, wipe the blade with a disinfectant and dry it thoroughly.

Cutting Boards
Cutting boards are essential for food preparation, but they can also harbor bacteria. Over time, knives can create tiny grooves and scratches in the surface of the cutting board, which can trap bacteria. If you use the same cutting board for raw meat and vegetables, you can spread bacteria from the meat to the vegetables.

Wash wooden cutting boards in hot, soapy water after each use. Rinse thoroughly and dry with a clean towel. Never put wooden cutting boards in the dishwasher, as this can damage the wood. Plastic or glass cutting boards can be washed in the dishwasher.

Sponges
Sponges are a breeding ground for bacteria. The porous structure of a sponge makes it easy for bacteria to grow.

Rinse sponges thoroughly after each use and allow them to air dry. You can also microwave sponges for a few minutes to kill bacteria. Replace sponges frequently.

Knobs, Handles, and Light Switches
How often do you clean the knobs and handles on your kitchen cabinets? What about the handles on your refrigerator and the light switches in your kitchen? These surfaces can be a breeding ground for bacteria.

Wipe down knobs, handles, and light switches with a disinfectant cleaner regularly.

Gas Leaks and Carbon Monoxide
If you have gas appliances in your kitchen, it's important to make sure they're properly maintained. A gas leak can be dangerous, and carbon monoxide is a silent killer.

If you smell gas, evacuate your home immediately and call the gas company. If you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning, get fresh air and call 911.

Plastic Containers
Plastic containers are a convenient way to store food, but not all plastics are created equal. Some older plastics contain bisphenol A (BPA), a chemical that has been linked to health problems.

When choosing plastic containers, look for BPA-free options.

Microwave Popcorn
Microwave popcorn is a convenient snack, but it can also be a source of unhealthy chemicals. The chemicals used to flavor microwave popcorn can be released into the air when the bag is heated.

When making microwave popcorn, open the bag carefully and avoid inhaling the fumes.

Reusable Grocery Bags
Reusable grocery bags are a great way to reduce waste, but they can also be a source of bacteria. If you use reusable grocery bags, be sure to wash them regularly.

Wash reusable grocery bags in hot water with soap.

By taking a few simple steps, you can make your kitchen a safer and healthier place.

Nekateri v težavah lahko povzročijo prebavne motnje v nekaj dneh, drugi pa so lahko smrtni, zlasti za majhne otroke in tiste z oslabljenim imunskim sistemom. Če se počutite slabo, je čas, da si ogledate svojo kuhinjo in morda spremenite nekatere navade.
Nepravilno ravnanje s hrano
Ena največjih nevarnosti za zdravje v vaši kuhinji ste vi in kako ravnate s hrano. Če hrane ne kuhamo in ne ravnamo varno, se bakterije lahko hitro razmnožujejo, kar povzroča bolezni, ki se prenašajo s hrano, ki segajo od nekaj ur prebavne motnje do smrti.
Ste krivi za katero koli od teh napak?
- Premajhna hrana : Hrano je treba spraviti na primerno temperaturo, ki je potrebna za uničenje bakterij. Ritni rumenjaki, suši ali surovo testo za piškote so še posebej nevarni za majhne otroke ali vse, ki imajo oslabljen imunski sistem.
- Prepuščanje ostankov pri napačni temperaturi : Nepravilna temperatura hrane preprosto povabi bakterije, kvas in plesen, da uspevajo. Vroča hrana mora biti hranjena nad 140 stopinj F, hladna hrana pa pod 40 stopinj F. To vključuje živila, ki jih odtajamo ali mariniramo. Te hrane nikoli ne puščajte na pultu dlje časa. Odtajajte počasi v hladilniku ali hitreje v mikrovalovni pečici in takoj uporabite.
- Uporaba nepranega izdelka : Vse sveže izdelke je treba oprati pred jedjo ali uporabiti pri kuhanju, da odstranite bakterije in pesticide.
- Izpiranje surovega mesa : Surovega mesa pred kuhanjem ne smete oprati. Pranje ali izpiranje surovega mesa v pomivalnem koritu preprosto razširi vse bakterije na korito in pulti. Kuhanje na ustrezni temperaturi bo ubilo potencialno škodljive bakterije.
- Navzkrižna kontaminacija med surovo in kuhano hrano : Nikoli ne uporabljajte iste plošče za mariniranje surovega mesa ali ga odnesite na žar, ki ga uporabljate za postrežbo končnega izdelka. V trgovinah shranjujte surovo hrano ločeno v nakupovalni košarici od pripravljenih živil. Doma shranjujte surove izdelke v neprepustnih vrečah in stran od pripravljenih živil v hladilniku ali shrambi.
- Preskakovanje pranja rok med kuhanjem : Ko se premikate po korakih priprave hrane, si pogosto umijte roke, še posebej po obdelavi mesa, jajc in svežih izdelkov.
Razvajena hrana
Skoraj vsi imamo v hladilniku ali shrambi nekaj hrane, ki jo je treba metati. Jesti ali kuhati s hrano, ki je pretekla čas varnega skladiščenja, je izjemno nevarna. Če ste previdni pri hrani, jo vrzite. Ne okusite! Vse bakterije, ki lahko povzročijo zastrupitev s hrano, ni mogoče okusiti, videti ali vonjati.
Preprečevanje zastrupitve s hrano se začne, ko nakupujete. Izberite sadje in zelenjavo, ki se ne poškoduje ali kaže znake škode žuželk. Ne kupujte konzerviranih predmetov, ki so nabrekli, zgubani ali zarjaveli po šivih. Pakirani predmeti ne smejo imeti solz ali znakov madežev zaradi puščanja.
Brisače
Tkanine za kuhinjske brisače so bistven in odličen način za zmanjšanje uporabe papirnatih brisač. Nevarnost pride, če jih ne umivate dovolj pogosto in povzroča navzkrižno kontaminacijo na kuhinjskih površinah. Glede na raziskavo National Sanitation Foundation International je vsaj 75 odstotkov kuhinjskih brisač testiralo bakterije koliformne bakterije (Salmonella ali E.coli).
Za čiščenje, pripravo hrane in pranje rok uporabljajte ločene brisače. Brisače operemo po vroči vodi po vsaki uporabi.
Odpirači
Ne glede na to, ali uporabljate ročni ali električni odpirač pločevinke, je rezilo vsakič izpostavljeno vsebini pločevinke. Navzkrižna kontaminacija mesnih izdelkov, zelenjave in pijač lahko povzroči rast bakterij.

Storms and anticyclones relate to different pressures in the atmosphere. Atmospheric pressure is measured in millibars (mbar). A millibar is equal to one-thousandth of a bar, and a bar is equal to 1 atmosphere (atm). It is important to understand what a millibar means, as a difference of more or less millibars in a region creates storms and anticyclones.
Before delving into the details, anticyclones and storms can be easily identified on a map by considering isobars. If the pressure is higher than usual, for example, 1024 mb, then we are talking about an anticyclone. When the pressure is low, for example, 996 millibars, as shown in the picture, we are talking about a storm. From here, the climate associated with different pressures varies.
Anticyclone
Usually, it can be compared to stable weather, with clear skies and sunshine. Its pressure is approximately 1016 millibars or higher.
The air in an anticyclone is more stable than the air around it. On the other hand, air descends from the atmosphere, creating a phenomenon known as “subsidence.” Subsidence, as such, prevents the formation of precipitation. The way the air descends varies depending on the hemisphere we are in. In the Northern Hemisphere, it rotates downwards in a clockwise direction. And in the Southern Hemisphere, it is exactly the opposite.
Storm
In contrast to an anticyclone, it is associated with unstable weather, cloudy skies, and precipitation. Its pressure is less than 1016 millibars.
The direction of air rotation in a storm, which in this case rises upwards, does so in the opposite direction of an anticyclone. That is, in a clockwise direction in the Southern Hemisphere and in a counter-clockwise direction in the Northern Hemisphere.
They usually bring winds and lower the temperature, both in summer and winter. They usually occur due to the entry of fewer solar rays, as they are reflected by the clouds and prevented from passing through.

Clean, drinkable water is more precious than gold – it is essential for human life. Unfortunately, population growth and pollution threaten to seriously compromise the availability of clean drinking water. According to available data, the costs of water treatment have increased.
Maintaining the quality of clean drinking water for people is becoming an increasingly challenging task, requiring not only the financial resources for expensive treatment in case of contamination, but also the construction of new drinking water treatment plants.
There are three main elements responsible for water pollution: sediment, nitrogen, and phosphorus, which accumulate in watersheds from which we obtain our drinking water. These pollutants can enter watersheds for various reasons, but they all share one thing in common: human activities that can have a significant impact on the quality of drinking water.
The following are just a few examples.
Agriculture
Agriculture contributes significantly to water pollution through the use of fertilizers (including those from biogas plants) and the large amounts of manure produced by livestock. Intensive dairy farming can contaminate groundwater in nearby areas, increasing nitrate levels in drinking water above permissible limits. Elevated nitrate levels in water can cause serious health problems for both infants and adults with weakened immune systems.
Another source of pollution is the industrial production of crops, such as corn, which relies heavily on fertilizers to increase yields. This fertilization can lead to the growth of harmful algae in waterways and water sources. These algae are toxic and, in severe cases, can even necessitate the closure of entire water supply networks. When fertilizers are used excessively, the soil in fields and meadows cannot absorb them, and the excess fertilizer ends up in streams, rivers, and, ultimately, lakes and seas. This excess fertilizer is largely responsible for toxic algal blooms.
Fossil fuel production
The production of electricity from fossil fuels is another human activity that significantly impacts drinking water quality.
Consider the use of coal, which can have serious consequences for water quality. Coal ash, a byproduct of burning coal for electricity generation, is one of the largest forms of waste. This ash contains hazardous elements, such as arsenic and mercury, as well as radioactive substances. If this ash is not properly stored, it can contaminate groundwater.
Coal ash in a pond at a thermal power plant.
Sewage
In some areas, rapid population growth has outpaced the capacity of existing sewage treatment plants, which were designed for a smaller population. As a result, they are no longer able to adequately treat wastewater.
The situation is even worse in areas where the government allows industrial zones to be developed without adequate sewage infrastructure. Untreated wastewater flows directly into groundwater, streams, and lakes, eventually reaching drinking water sources.
Development
Development also requires changes in land use, converting agricultural land into industrial areas. According to our legislation, planners are only required to assess the environmental impact of individual facilities, but they are not required to consider the impact of other facilities on that facility or on nature. This narrow approach to planning can lead to an overload of water infrastructure and, consequently, a domino effect of water pollution.
The most absurd example is when planners build a main sewage line above a water collection area, because they are convinced that the sewage pipes are so high quality that they will never be damaged – not by quality, not by earthquakes, not by vibrations from traffic infrastructure. If even one pipe bursts, residents in that area will be drinking water contaminated with sewage.
Will we be forced to drink only bottled water?
Deforestation, which often occurs to make way for agriculture and development, also contributes significantly to sediment pollution in drinking water.
Climate change
The bad news is that climate change will exacerbate many of the problems that already threaten our water resources in some areas. Decreasing rainfall in the summer will lead to more frequent and severe droughts, negatively impacting the availability of water resources. We can expect longer periods of drought and shorter, more localized periods of intense rainfall. As a result, flood patterns will change, average low flows in rivers will decrease, and we can also expect problems with water supply due to falling groundwater levels or the depletion of groundwater reserves below existing levels.

Let a1, a2, a3, ... be a sequence of positive real numbers. Suppose that for some positive integer s, we have
an = max{ak + an−k | 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1}
for all n > s. Prove that there exist positive integers ℓ and N, with ℓ ≤ s and such that an = aℓ + an−ℓ for all n ≥ N.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Many people experience a runny nose when exposed to cold air. This happens to between 50 and 90 percent of people, and the phenomenon is called cold-induced rhinitis or "ski nose." People who suffer from asthma, hay fever, and skin rashes are particularly susceptible, according to the ScienceAlert portal.
"When we breathe through our nose and the outside temperature is below zero, the air coming from the nasal cavity and on its way to the lungs usually reaches a temperature of 26, sometimes 30 degrees Celsius. At this point, the humidity is more than one hundred percent, regardless of how cold the air we are inhaling is. All of this demonstrates the effectiveness of the nose. It ensures that the air we breathe becomes warm and moist in the lungs," the professor explained.
Cold and dry air stimulate nerve endings in the nose, which send a message to the brain. The brain, this important organ, responds to the message by increasing blood flow to the nose.
Therefore, the brain responds to this impulse by increasing blood flow to the nose, and these dilated blood vessels warm the air that passes by them. At the same time, the nose is stimulated to produce a larger amount of mucus through the mucous membrane to ensure sufficient moisture to humidify the incoming air.
Cold, dry air also irritates immune system cells (called mast cells) in the nose. These cells trigger the production of more fluid in the nose to humidify the air. It is estimated that between 300 and 400 milliliters of fluid are lost through the nose during this process each day.
Heat and water loss are closely linked: warming the air in the nasal cavity means that the lining of the nasal cavity becomes cooler than body temperature; at the same time, water evaporates to humidify the air. The evaporation of water, which requires a large amount of heat, draws heat from the nose and thus cools it.
The body is aware of its priorities.
Essentially, the body is aware of its priorities: consequently, blood flow to the nose is further increased, as warming the inhaled air takes precedence over heat loss from the nose (the body's usual response to cold is to divert blood away from the surface into deep vessels, thereby minimizing heat loss through the skin).
It is therefore a matter of finding a balance to achieve the right amount of heat and moisture loss from the nose.
When this balance is disrupted, the compensatory mechanism becomes somewhat overactive, and the excess moisture, which is not needed to humidify the cold, dry air, drips from the nostrils. Dr. Kralj points out that "dripping" from the nose is a natural physiological phenomenon, as "increased secretion is necessary for better humidification and cleaning of the air in a cold environment."
In general, immune system cells, or mast cells, are usually more sensitive in people with asthma and allergies, and blood vessels respond more in those who are more sensitive to environmental irritants and temperature changes. Thus, cold air can trigger nasal congestion and even sneezing.

Mnogim ljudem začne teči z nosu, ko pridejo na hladen zrak. Dogaja se med 50 do 90. tim odstotkom ljudi, pojav pa se imenuje rinitis zaradi mrazu ali "smučarski nos". Še posebej so k temu nagnjeni ljudje, ki trpijo zaradi astme, senenega nahoda in zaradi izpuščaja, poroča portal ScienceAlert.
"Ko dihamo skozi nos in je zunanja temperatura pod ničlo, zrak, ki prihaja iz nosne votline in je na svoji poti do pljuč, običajno doseže temperaturo 26, včasih 30 stopinj Celzija. Vlažnost je v tem trenutku več kot sto odstotna ne glede na to, kako hladen je zrak, ki ga ob tem vdihavamo. Vse to dokazuje na učinkovitos nosu. Ta nam zagotavlja, da zrak, ki ga dihamo, v pljučih postane topel in vlažen," je pojasnil profesor.
Hladni in suhi zrak stimulirata živčne končnice v nosu, ti pošiljajo sporočilo možganom. Možgani, ta pomemben organ se odzove na sporočilo tako, da povečuje cirkulacijo v nosu.
Možgani se torej na ta impulz odzovej povečanim pretoko krvi do nosu in te razširjene krvne žile segrevajo zrak, ki potuje mimo njih. Nos ob tem dobi povod za proizvodnjo večje količine izločka preko sluznice, da bi zagotovil zadostno vlago za navlaženje zraka, ki prihaja skozi.
Hladen suh zrak obenem tudi draži celice imunskega sistema (imenovane mastociti) v nosu. Te celice sprožijo proizvodnjo večje količine tekočine v nosu za vlaženje zraka. Po ocenah naj bi med tem procesom skozi nos dnevno izgubili med 300 in 400 mililitri tekočine.
Vročina in izguba vode sta tesno povezani: segrevanje zraka v nosni votlini pomeni, da postane obloga nosne votline hladnejša od telesne temperature; hkrati voda izhlapeva, da bi se zrak navlažil. Izhlapevanje vode, za katerega so potrebne velike količine vročine, toploto jemlje iz nosu in ga na tak način hladi.
Telo se zaveda svojih prednostnih nalog
V bistvu se telo se zaveda prednostnih nalog: posledično se še bolj poveča pretok krvi v nos, saj ima segrevanje vdihnjenega zraka prednost pred izgubo toplote iz nosu (običajni odziv telesa na mraz je, da spelje kri proč od površja v globoke žile in s tem kar se da zmanjša izgubo toplote skozi kožo).
Gre torej za lovljenje ravnotežja, da bi dosegli pravilno količino toplote in izgubo vlage iz nosu.
Ko je to ravnovesje moteno, je kompenzacijski mehanizem nekoliko preveč aktiven, čezmerna vlaga, ki ni potrebna za vlaženje tega mrzlega, suhega zraka, kaplja iz nosnic. Dr. Kralj opozarja, da je "kapljanje" iz nosu naravni fiziološki pojav, saj je "povečano izločanje odvajanja vode potrebno za boljše vlaženje in čiščenje zraka v hladnem okolju."
Sicer so celice imunskega sistema ali mestociti običajano bolj bolj občutljivi pri ljudeh z astmo in alergijami, krvne žile pa se bolj odzivajo pri tistih, ki so bolj občutljivi na dražljaje iz okolice in temperaturne spremembe. Tako lahko hladen zrak sproži prenapolnjenost nosu in celo kihanje.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Every organism is occasionally targeted by other organisms. As a response, we have evolved a wide range of defense strategies throughout evolution. The immune system (Latin: immunis = free) protects us against insidious disease-causing microorganisms, viruses, parasites, and even cancer cells.

The immune system recognizes bacteria and viruses that manage to penetrate the first line of defense – the physical barrier of the skin and mucous membranes – as foreign invaders and destroys them. The immune system is capable of detecting foreign bodies, reacting, and remembering them.

The immune system is one of the most complex systems in our body. It has its own circulatory system – lymphatic vessels – which supply all organs except the brain.

Lymph flows through the lymphatic vessels, containing white blood cells (lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils) and fat droplets. The immune system also consists of other specialized molecules, such as cytokines and antibodies.

There are specific locations – lymph nodes, tonsils, the spleen, bone marrow, the spleen, the liver, and the intestines – where white blood cells gather, organize, and are directed to specific locations where their help is needed. For example, if a wound from a cut on your finger becomes infected, it will soon cause enlarged lymph nodes in your elbow, or if your throat is infected, you will notice enlarged lymph nodes under your lower jaw. Lymph nodes swell because the lymph drains infectious particles, such as microbes, into nearby lymph nodes. Here, lymphocytes filter, attack, and destroy them.

What is the function of the immune system?
The entire system combines its forces to detect, recognize, and destroy substances that are harmful to the organism.

The main function of the immune system is to protect the body from various infections and malignant diseases and to regulate the healing process. This is made possible by its ability to recognize "self" and "non-self."

A weakened immune system is a cause of people becoming ill more quickly from various viral infections (e.g., colds, flu), bacterial and fungal infections, and malignant diseases, and wounds heal more slowly. Conversely, there are conditions in which the immune system functions more strongly than necessary. This can lead to various allergic reactions, chronic inflammatory diseases, or autoimmune diseases (e.g., diabetes, lupus, psoriasis), in which the immune system no longer distinguishes between "self" and "non-self" and therefore attacks its own cells in the inflammation.

The most important function of any organism is to maintain internal balance (homeostasis). A change in this balance can occur, for example, when a large amount of free radicals is released in the body due to contact with the influenza virus, which is one form of defense.

In a normal immune response, the amount of antioxidants increases, neutralizing the action of free radicals and maintaining balance. If the body cannot provide enough antioxidants (this is often the case in older people and those with chronic diseases), oxidative stress occurs, which can directly destroy cells or cause their apoptosis (programmed cell death). Oxidative stress can be one of the most important causes of damage to the function of all cells, including immune system cells.

The immune system can be weakened by stress, fatigue, smoking, poor diet, lack of physical activity, and insufficient time spent in fresh air. Age is also a significant factor.

The immune systems of infants and young children are still underdeveloped. A cold that doesn't affect adults can manifest in a severe form in children. Many older people also have a reduced ability of their immune system to defend the body against infections and remove abnormal cells. However, not all older people are affected. In some, the immune system remains as active as it was in their youth. Therefore, we cannot ignore the genetic factor.

Children are more susceptible and get colds more quickly because their immune systems are not yet fully developed. They are more likely to infect each other and transmit diseases to their families.

What is the best way to protect your immune system, increase your resistance, and avoid infections?

Doctor's offices are usually full in winter and early spring. Most patients come to the doctor with the flu or a cold. You wake up healthy in the morning and go to work, but in the evening, you may already have a fever and feel ill.

1. Healthy skin and mucous membranes are the first line of defense against the invasion of harmful microorganisms that surround us. Dry skin and mucous membranes have a poorer defense capacity. Drink enough water. Instead of staying indoors, go outside. Ventilate your home regularly and, if possible, install a humidifier. When the sun shines on cold days, quickly go out and enjoy its rays. Avoid walking in the city when it is foggy and humid, and in summer when it is too hot.
2. Moderate physical activity strengthens our body and is the basis of a healthy lifestyle. It is recommended to do 30 minutes of exercise per day until you sweat or breathe heavily. Overdoing it is not recommended and has the opposite effect, as the body needs more time to restore internal balance, and in the meantime, it is more susceptible to infections.
Moderate physical activity reduces the negative impact of stress on resistance, improves the circulation of white blood cells throughout the body, and strengthens the cardiovascular system. If you have not been physically active until now, start with a 30-minute walk and brisk walk three to four times a week.
3. Improve your diet.
Inadequate nutrition, poor in nutrients, vitamins, and minerals, first affects cellular immune resistance, which depends on T lymphocytes. Research has shown that vitamins C, A, E, B6, and certain minerals – iron, zinc, and selenium – play a key role.
With food, we can provide the body with all the necessary substances to regulate and improve the function of the immune system in defense against infections. The general rules of a healthy diet also apply here. Eat fruits and vegetables five times a day, with each meal. If you cannot always afford fresh fruit, choose frozen fruit instead of canned fruit. The latter has fewer vitamins and too much added sugar.
Eat more green leafy vegetables (such as cabbage, spinach, lettuce), orange vegetables and fruits (citrus fruits, dried apricots, pumpkins, carrots, etc.), peppers, avocados, whole-grain foods, whole-grain cereals, seafood, fish, and red meat.
Eat sweets only on special occasions, as they provide the body with excess calories. A diet high in sugar weakens the ability of white blood cells to defend against viruses and pathogens and can significantly weaken the immune system.
Avoid fatty foods and fried foods. However, you do not need to limit the consumption of foods that contain unsaturated fatty acids (found in fish – especially sardines, mackerel, tuna, salmon), nuts, and seeds. It is recommended to eat fish two to three times a week.
4. Drink more fluids.
The best are water and unsweetened herbal teas. It is recommended to reduce the amount of coffee, tea, and alcohol consumed.
5. Get enough sleep.
During good sleep, the body replenishes its energy. Some tips for better sleep and pleasant dreams will not be superfluous. Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day. Avoid napping during the day, as this will make it difficult to sleep at night. It is recommended to eat something light before going to bed, such as a banana, a glass of milk, or yogurt. To fall asleep peacefully, make a plan for the next day before going to bed. Ventilate the bedroom before going to bed and make sure it is not too hot. Keep it tidy and arrange it so that you feel comfortable in it (pleasant lighting, wall color, nice bedding, etc.).
6. Open the windows, as well-ventilated rooms stop the spread of microorganisms in the air.
7. Vitamins and minerals
The following antioxidants are especially important for resistance to the flu and colds: vitamin C (found in citrus fruits, potatoes, peppers, tomatoes, cabbage, etc.), vitamin E (dried fruit, sunflower seeds, nuts, etc.), vitamin A (liver, egg yolk, cheese, butter), beta-carotene (carrots, spinach, lettuce, apricots, melons, tomatoes), zinc (red meat, fish, seafood, eggs, nuts, cereals, liver), selenium (cereals, meat, fish).
The immune system of older people is more sensitive to nutritional deficiencies. Age-related immune dysfunction can be alleviated with appropriate dietary supplements. Even if you cannot ensure a proper diet, take vitamin and mineral supplements in winter.
In summer, take advantage of the warm and pleasant morning and afternoon sun and get plenty of vitamin D.
8. Avoid stress.
Stress has a strong impact on the immune system. The impact can be twofold. In most cases, it inhibits the functions of the immune system, but sometimes it has the opposite effect and is stimulating. Short-term stress (e.g., injury) has a beneficial effect on the immune system because it mobilizes white blood cells to reach the damaged tissue where they are needed and the body restores its original balance. Long-term, chronic stress inhibits the immune system. Positive changes in the immune system are replaced by negative ones. First at the cellular level, and then in a broader sense. During adaptation to long-term stress, changes occur in function (hyper- or hypo-activity) or damage to cells, tissues, and organs.
9. Wash your hands as often as possible during the day. This is especially important during epidemics. Viruses can survive for several hours on the skin or on objects such as doorknobs, doors, towels, etc.
10. If you have a severe cold, stay home and rest. You will recover faster and will not infect other people.
The global and personal goal in preventing infectious diseases is to do everything possible to ensure the functioning of your own, unique mechanisms for resistance to disease.

Prepared by: Nataša Jan, MSc, University Diploma in Biology.

Vsak organizem je občasno tarča napada drugih organizmov. Kot odgovor na to smo skozi evolucijo razvili najrazličnejše obrambne strategije. Obrambo proti zahrbtnim bolezenskim mikroorganizmom, virusom, zajedalcem pa tudi rakavim celicam, nam omogoča imunski sistem (latinsko: immunis = osvobojen).
Bakterije in viruse, ki se jim uspe prebiti skozi prvo obrambno linijo – fizično oviro kože in sluznic, imunski sistem spozna kot tuje napadalce in jih uniči. Imunski sistem je namreč sposoben odkrivati tuja telesca, reagirati in si zapomniti.
Imunski sistem je eden najbolj zapletenih sistemov v našem telesu. Ima svoja lastna obtočila – limfne žile, ki oskrbujejo vse organe, razen možganov.
Po limfnih žilah se pretaka limfa, ki vsebuje bele krvničke (limfocite, makrofage, nevtrofilce) in maščobne kapljice. Imunski sistem sestavljajo tudi druge specializirane molekule kot so citokini in protitelesca.
Obstajajo posebna mesta – bezgavke, mandlji, priželjc, kostni mozeg, vranica, jetra, črevo, kjer se bele krvničke zberejo, organizirajo in usmerijo na določena mesta, kjer je potrebna njihova pomoč. Na primer, če se nam rana po urezu prsta na roki okuži, kmalu povzroči povečane bezgavke na komolcu ali pri okužbi žrela opazimo povečanje bezgavk pod spodnjo čeljustjo. Bezgavke otečejo, ker limfa odvaja kužne delce, kot so na primer mikrobi, v bližnje bezgavke. Tu jih limfociti filtrirajo, napadajo in uničujejo.
Kaj je naloga imunskega sistema
Celoten sistem torej združuje svoje moči v odkrivanju, prepoznavanju in uničevanju za organizem škodljivih snovi.
Glavna naloga imunskega sistema je, da telo ščiti pred različnimi infekcijami, malignimi obolenji in da regulira proces celjenja. To mu omogoča sposobnost, da prepozna »lastno« in »tuje«.
Oslabljeni imunski sistem je vzrok, da človek hitreje zboli zaradi različnih virusnih okužb (npr. prehladi, gripa), bakterijskih in glivičnih okužb, malignih obolenj, počasneje se celijo rane. Nasprotno temu, pa obstajajo stanja, ko imunski sitem deluje močneje kot je potrebno. Takrat pride do različnih alergijskih reakcij, kroničnih vnetnih bolezni ali pa do avtoimunskih bolezni (npr. diabetes, lupus, psoriaza), ko imunski sistem ne loči več »lastnega« od »tujega« ter zato v vsej vnemi prične napadati celo lastne celice.
Najvažnejša funkcija vsakega organizma je vzdrževanje notranjega ravnotežja (homeostaze). Do spremembe v tem ravnotežju lahko pride, ko se na primer zaradi stika z virusom gripe, v telesu osvobodi velika količina prostih radikalov, kar je ena od oblik obrambe.
Pri normalnem imunskem odgovoru se poveča količina antioksidantov, ki nevtralizirajo delovanje prostih radikalov in ravnotežje se obdrži. V primeru, da telo ne more zagotoviti dovolj antioksidantov (to je pogosto pri starejših ljudeh, kroničnih bolnikih), pride do oksidativnega stresa, ki lahko direktno uniči celico ali pa povzroči njeno apoptozo (programirano smrt celice). Oksidativni stres je lahko eden od najvažnejših vzrokov poškodbe funkcije vseh celic, tudi celic imunskega sistema.
Imunski sistem lahko oslabi zaradi stresa, utrujenosti, kajenja, nepravilnega načina prehrane, premajhne telesne dejavnosti in nezadostnega gibanja na svežem zraku. Bistveni dejavnik je tudi starost.
Imunski sistem dojenčkov in mlajših otrok je še nezadostno razvit. Prehlad, ki se odraslih niti ne dotakne, se lahko pri otrocih izrazi v hudi obliki. Tudi pri mnogih starejših ljudeh je sposobnost imunskega sistema, da brani telo pred okužbami in odstranjuje abnormalne celice, zmanjšana. Vendar pa vsi starejši niso prizadeti. Pri nekaterih imunski sistem ostaja enako aktiven kot v mladosti. Torej tudi genetskega dejavnika ne moremo prezreti.
Otroci so bolj občutljivi in se hitreje prehladijo, ker njihov imunski sistem še ni dokončno razvit. Lažje okužijo drug drugega in bolezni prenesejo na svoje domače.
Kako najbolje zavarujemo svoj imunski sistem ter povečamo odpornost in se izognemo okužbam ?
Zdravniške ordinacije so sploh pozimi in zgodaj spomladi prepolne. Večina bolnikov pride k zdravniku zaradi gripe in prehlada. Zjutraj vstanemo zdravi in gremo v službo, zvečer pa nas že lahko trese mrzlica, vročina naraste, zbolimo.
1. Zdrava koža in sluznice so prva obrambna linija proti vdoru škodljivih mikroorganizmov, ki nas obkrožajo. Presuha koža in sluznice imajo slabšo obrambno sposobnost. Pijmo dovolj vode. Namesto da se zapiramo v stanovanja, raje pojdimo na zrak. Stanovanja redno prezračujemo po možnosti pa vanj namestimo ustrezen vlažilec zraka. Kadar v mrzlih dneh posije sonce, se hitro odpravimo na lov za njegovimi žarki. Izogibajmo se sprehodom po mestu, kadar je megleno in vlažno vreme ter poleti kadar je vročina previsoka.
2. Zmerna telesna dejavnost krepi naše telo in je temelj zdravega načina življenja. Priporočljivo je 30 minut gibanja na dan, dokler se ne oznojimo ali zadihamo. Pretiravanje ni priporočljivo in daje nasproten učinek, saj telo potrebuje veliko več časa, da vzpostavi notranje ravnotežje, medtem pa je bolj občutljivo na okužbe.
Zmerna telesna dejavnost blaži negativno delovanje stresa na odpornost, boljše je kroženje belih krvničk po telesu, krepi krvožilni sistem. V primeru, da doslej niste bili telesno dejavni, začnite s 30 minutnim sprehodom in hitro hojo, trikrat do štirikrat tedensko.
3. Izboljšajmo način prehrane
Nezadostna in s hranilnimi snovmi, vitamini in minerali revna prehrana najprej prizadene celično imunsko odpornost, ki je odvisna od limfocitov T. Raziskave so pokazale, da igrajo ključno vlogo predvsem vitaminov C, A, E, B6 in nekateri minerali: železo, cink in selen.
S hrano lahko telesu zagotovimo vse potrebne snovi za uravnavanje in izboljšanje delovanja imunskega sistema, v obrambi proti okužbam. Tudi tu veljajo splošna pravila zdravega načina prehrane. Sadje in zelenjavo naj bi jedli petkrat na dan, to je pri vsakem obroku. V primeru, da si vedno ne moremo zagotoviti svežega sadja, rajši izberimo zamrznjeno kakor vloženo sadje. Slednje ima manj vitaminov in preveč dodanega sladkorja.
Še posebno jejmo več zelene listnate zelenjave (kot je npr. zelje, špinača, solata). oranžne zelenjave in sadja (agrumi, posušene marelice, buče, korenje,idr.), papriko, avokado, živila iz polnozrnate moke, polnozrnate kosmiče, morske sadeže, ribe, rdeče meso.
Sladkarije jejmo le ob posebnih priložnostih saj z njimi v telo vnašamo odvečne kalorije. Prehrana z veliko sladkorja slabi sposobnost belih krvnih celic za obrambo proti virusom in bolezenskim klicam in lahko precej oslabi delovanje imunskega sistema.
Izogibati se je potrebno mastni hrani in cvrtju. Ni pa treba omejevati uživanja hrane, ki vsebuje nenasičene maščobne kisline (so v ribah – predvsem sardinah, skušah, tuni, lososu), oreščkih in semenih. Ribe je priporočljivo jesti dvakrat do trikrat na teden.
4. Pijmo več tekočine.
Najboljša je voda in nesladkani zeliščni čaji. Zmanjšati je priporočljivo količino popite kave, pravega čaja in alkohola.
5. Dobro se naspimo
Med dobrim spancem si telo nabere novih moči. Nekaj nasvetov za boljše spanje in lepše sanje ne bo odveč. Spati odhajajmo vedno ob isti uri in ob isti uri vstanimo. Dremanje podnevi raje izpustimo, saj drugače ne bomo dobro spali ponoči. Pred spanjem je priporočljivo pojesti kaj lahkega, na primer banano, kozarec mleka ali jogurta. As people age, the risk of developing diseases such as diabetes, cancer, sarcopenia (loss of muscle mass), bone loss, weakened immune system, and cognitive decline increases.
Scientists studying aging are not only interested in the mechanisms that lead all organisms to decline and eventually die, but also in how to extend lifespan without compromising its quality. In other words, how to stay healthy and live longer.
One of the mechanisms that has been studied for some time in simple organisms such as yeast and some invertebrates, as well as in different strains and species of rodents, is restricting energy intake. Consistently lower energy intake, without causing malnutrition, delays the onset of age-related diseases.
Energy restriction has also been studied in rhesus macaques, which are an excellent model for studying human aging, as these monkeys share 93% of their genetic code with humans, and consequently, many anatomical, physiological, and neurological characteristics, as well as similar endocrine and immune systems. It affects the (later) onset of sarcopenia, osteoporosis, and arthritis, reduces the likelihood of cancer and cardiovascular diseases, and, most importantly, appears to prolong the body's ability to regulate blood sugar levels effectively.

Increased expression of NLRP3 is a major driver of the inflammatory response in autoimmune diseases and autoinflammatory diseases, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's disease, and atherosclerosis.

High blood pressure, or hypertension, is a cardiovascular disorder that occurs when there are problems with blood flow throughout the body, either due to narrowed arteries or some other type of obstruction.
When this problem arises, the heart has to work twice as hard to pump blood through the smaller spaces, which increases the pressure.
Some call it a "silent killer" because it is asymptomatic in its early stages, and many people ignore the problem until they experience more serious consequences.
Although it doesn't cause major damage at first, over time it causes changes in other systems in the body and can lead to serious illness.
Next, we will explain in detail the 8 complications that can occur when hypertension is left untreated.
1. Heart Attack
A heart attack is one of the serious illnesses associated with uncontrolled high blood pressure.
This condition, which can become fatal, occurs because the arteries harden and narrow, affecting blood flow.
See also: 8 Bad Habits for Heart Health
2. Stroke
Strokes can occur when blood flow is restricted to one of the points that allows it to reach the brain.
Because pressure directly affects blood circulation to this vital organ, patients with hypertension are very likely to develop this pathology.
3. Heart Failure
Heart failure is related to the excessive effort the heart has to make to pump blood through hardened, narrow arteries.
In fact, this condition is one of the leading causes of death among those with hypertension, as it directly affects the heart muscle.
Among its symptoms, we can highlight, for example:
- Difficulty breathing
- Swelling of the extremities
- Abdominal tension
- Difficulty sleeping
- Urinary incontinence
- Fatigue or feeling weak
4. Diabetes
Unlike other disorders caused by uncontrolled blood pressure, diabetes can be either a result or a cause.
Uncontrolled blood sugar levels can affect blood flow and arterial health, as well as interfere with the proper passage of blood to the heart.
But the pressure caused by other factors can also affect both blood, even reducing the ability to use sugars as an energy source.
Diabetes often worsens in patients with hypertension because pressure affects metabolism, as well as the function of the pancreas and kidneys.
5. Atherosclerosis
Atherosclerosis is a condition that occurs when high blood pressure remains without any significant treatment.
This leads to hardening of the arteries, which can lead to dangerous blockages and disorders, such as coronary artery disease.
6. Kidney Disease
The kidneys are designed to filter waste products from the blood, regulate electrolytes, and excrete excess fluids through urine.
Hypertension directly affects its functions, limiting blood flow, which allows it to work properly.
Over time, kidney health deteriorates significantly, reducing oxygenation and the passage of nutrients to these organs.
In addition, peripheral arteries can become narrower, limiting its ability to remove waste, as well as creating irreversible damage and failure.

7. Eye Diseases
Many people don't realize how harmful high blood pressure is to vision health.
Restrictions in blood flow to any part of the body can cause damage to the retinal vessels.
In short, patients diagnosed with hypertension gradually develop eye diseases, starting with common symptoms such as inflammation, blurred vision, or loss of sharpness.
However, some medications used to manage the disease can significantly help reduce the symptoms of diseases such as hypertensive retinopathy.
Therefore, regular medical check-ups and appropriate tests are essential.
Finally, it is essential to pay close attention, especially when problems begin to appear in other systems of the body.

Natural climate solutions, sometimes called “nature-based solutions,” involve conserving, restoring, or better managing ecosystems to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere. Examples include allowing forests to regrow, restoring coastal wetlands and other wetlands, and shifting to regenerative agricultural practices, such as cover cropping, that support healthy soils. These ecosystems reduce climate change by capturing CO2 from the air and storing it in plants, soils, and sediments. They also provide a host of other important benefits, such as cleaner air and water, economic benefits, and increased biodiversity.
Some nature-based solutions, such as conserving existing wetlands, primarily prevent greenhouse gas emissions. Others, such as regenerative agriculture and reforestation, actively remove CO2 from the atmosphere, making them a form of carbon removal. (Many nature-based solutions both prevent emissions and remove carbon, so the distinction is blurry.) Nature-based carbon removal approaches are often presented as distinct from “engineered” approaches, such as bioenergy with carbon capture and storage, direct air capture with carbon storage, and ocean alkalinization. The distinction between nature-based solutions and engineered approaches, which some scholars have challenged, has important implications for carbon removal policy: the public generally supports approaches that they perceive as “natural.”
The Role of Natural Solutions in Climate Policy
Nature-based solutions can help reduce climate change, but they cannot “solve” climate change on their own: they need to be combined with rapid reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and potentially with engineered forms of carbon removal. Experts recently estimated that cost-effective nature-based solutions could contribute about 20% of the mitigation needed from now until 2050 to keep global warming below 2°C. The other 80% will need to come primarily from emissions reductions in the energy, transportation, building, and industrial sectors, and potentially from other carbon removal approaches. It is also important to note that any given area of forest or land can only store a limited amount of carbon. Once an area of land reaches that maximum carbon stock, it will no longer sequester additional carbon dioxide. This is another reason why nature-based solutions cannot replace emissions reductions.
Types of Natural Solutions
Nature-based solutions encompass a wide range of practices, and people sometimes disagree about what exactly counts as a nature-based solution. In general, nature-based solutions fall into four categories: forestry practices, wetland-related practices, regenerative agriculture, and ocean-based practices. Forestry practices include planting new forests, allowing forests to regrow naturally where they have been cut down, and improved forest management. Wetland-related practices focus on conserving and restoring peatlands, marshes, and coastal wetlands. Regenerative agriculture ranges from practices that build carbon in soils, such as no-till farming and cover cropping, to agroforestry and improved livestock management. Ocean-based practices include restoring seagrass meadows or cultivating algae or shellfish to restore or expand marine ecosystems.
Co-benefits and Concerns
- Biodiversity protection: Because they conserve or expand ecosystems, nature-based solutions protect biodiversity from climate change and habitat loss.
- Reversibility: Because they store carbon in biomass rather than in more permanent reservoirs, the carbon sequestration in nature-based solutions is reversible, meaning that the stored carbon could be released back into the atmosphere due to forest fires, changes in land use, or management practices.
- Co-benefits and concerns specific to individual methods: Different methods have different co-benefits, ranging from cleaner air and water to erosion control, flood protection, and more, as well as different concerns and challenges.
Management Considerations
- Awareness, education, and training: Many stakeholders may not be aware of the benefits of nature-based solutions or may need training to implement them properly.
- Financing and incentives: While many nature-based solutions pay for themselves over time, many potential adopters will need help with the upfront costs (e.g., new seedlings and equipment), and additional incentives can speed up adoption.
- Appropriate scale: Because some nature-based solutions, such as afforestation, compete with other land uses, good management can ensure that these solutions are implemented at an appropriate scale.
- Monitoring, reporting, and verification: Measuring and accounting for sequestered carbon can be challenging, but good management can streamline the process and help verify carbon storage.
- Protection of stored carbon: Good long-term management is needed to reduce the release of stored carbon back into the atmosphere.

Glucose, or blood sugar, provides our body and cells with a source of energy for daily activities. Since glucose supply depends on food intake, our body has developed mechanisms to maintain a constant glucose concentration in the blood. When food intake is reduced or absent, the body draws on its reserves to provide glucose to our cells. Conversely, when we have an excess, the body stores the energy. Hormones, including insulin, play a major role in these processes. Because these are quite complex regulatory mechanisms, glucagon, adrenaline, cortisol, and growth hormone also participate in this energy balance.

Insulin enables the storage of energy in the form of triglycerides and glycogen, inhibits the release of glucose from the liver into the blood, accelerates the formation and prevents the breakdown of proteins in muscles, and stimulates the formation and prevents the breakdown of fats in adipose tissue. Therefore, our body behaves economically and creates reserves if we don't consume as much as we ingest. But when does this balance begin to break down?

When there is a deficiency or disruption in one of the regulatory mechanisms involving the aforementioned hormones, the balance begins to break down, and the disease slowly develops. Depending on what happens, the glucose concentration in the blood chronically increases – hyperglycemia – which is diagnosed as diabetes. Based on the symptoms and how the disease develops, it is divided into type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

Type 1 develops very quickly, especially in childhood and adolescence (rarely later). Because in type 1, the problem is primarily at the level of the pancreas, where the so-called cells of the islets of Langerhans are deteriorating, and hyperglycemia appears when approximately 75% of the B cells are destroyed. Therefore, such patients need to receive insulin after rapid detection and diagnosis of the disease. Today, the pharmaceutical industry has made significant progress in the development of insulin preparations, pens for subcutaneous hormone application, as well as in the rapid development of insulin pumps, which allow the patient to adjust the insulin dose according to their current needs.

Type 2 is much more insidious because it develops very slowly and does not initially show typical signs. Type 2 can also be a consequence of certain other diseases (acute and chronic pancreatitis, some medications, thyroid diseases), as well as lifestyle (dietary habits, exercise), the presence of other diseases, and heredity. It arises due to insulin resistance in the tissues and its simultaneous reduced secretion. What disease signs should we be aware of: thirst, frequent need to urinate (especially at night), blurred vision, itchy skin, increased appetite… Some symptoms, especially in type 2, are not expressed so obviously that the disease can be detected early enough and thus protect the patient from late complications. These include primarily: damage to the heart, blood vessels, kidneys, eyes, and nervous system. What does this mean?

Damage to blood vessels first affects small vessels, which is called microangiopathy, and later also large vessels, which is called macroangiopathy. This is atherosclerosis, which, due to the presence of other risk factors (cholesterol, triglycerides, high blood pressure), means a significantly higher risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, or atherosclerosis of large vessels in the limbs with subsequent gangrene. Damage to the eyes due to diabetes is called retinopathy, where, due to the weakness of the capillaries, dilations and bleeding appear in the retina. Damage to the nervous system is called diabetic neuropathy, which manifests as peripheral (tingling in the legs, coldness, loss of sensation to touch and heat, burning feet, cramps,…) or neuropathy of the autonomic nervous system, which affects certain organs through the nerves.

A very serious complication is diabetic nephropathy, where, due to prolonged hyperglycemia, the renal tubules deteriorate, and kidney function fails.

As a chronic complication, we also know diabetic foot, where there is a combination of several factors mentioned above, changes in blood vessels (micro and macro) and nerves. Therefore, it is very important to detect the disease as early as possible, as this prevents or at least delays some of the aforementioned complications of diabetes.

The number of diabetic patients in the developed world is increasing rapidly.

What is the reason for the increase in the number of patients?

Partly, this is due to the increased life expectancy of the population, significantly greater access to food than in the past – obesity, which is increasing rapidly among the inhabitants of the old continent and North America, lack of exercise, as well as other diseases that lead to diabetes. Most worryingly, there is also obesity among children and adolescents, and thus the risk or even the development of type 2 diabetes.

- Has heart and blood vessel disease (atherosclerosis, elevated blood fats)
- Has diabetes in the family (parents, siblings,…)

To je ateroskleroza, ki pomeni še zaradi prisotnih drugih dejavnikov tveganja(holesterol, trigliceridi, povišan krvni tlak), bistveno večjo tveganje za koronarno srčno bolezen, možgansko kap ali aterosklerozo velikih žil na udih s posledično gangreno. Okvare na očesu zaradi sladkorne bolezni imenujemo retinopatija, kjer zaradi slabosti kapilar pojavijo razširitve in krvavitve v očesno mrežnico. Okvare živčnega sistema pa imenujemo diabetična nevropatija, ki se kaže kot periferna (mravljinci v nogah, mrazenje, izguba občutka za dotik in toploto, pekoče noge, krči,…) ali nevropatija avtonomnega živčevja, ki pa preko živčevja prizadene določene organe.
Zelo hud zaplet je diabetična nefropatija, zaradi dolgo trajajoče hiperglikemije pride do propada ledvičnih telesc in s tem odpoved ledvičnega delovanja.
Kot kronični zaplet poznamo še seveda diabetično stopalo, kjer imamo kombinacijo več dejavnikov prej zgoraj omenjenih sprememb na žilju (mikro in makro) in živčevju. Torej še kako pomembno je bolezen odkriti čim prej, saj tako preprečimo ali vsaj časovno preložimo nekaj od prej naštetih zapletov sladkorne bolezni.
Število sladkornih bolnikov, v razvitem svetu, strmo narašča.
Kaj je vzrok temu, da je število obolelih v porastu?
Delno je to podaljšana življenjska doba prebivalstva, bistveno večja dostopnost do hrane kot nekoč-debelost, ki je v močnem porastu med prebivalci stare celine kakor tudi Severne Amerike, premalo gibanja, kakor tudi druge bolezni, ki privedejo do sladkorne bolezni. Najbolj zaskrbljujoče je tudi debelost med otroci in mladostniki in s tem tveganje ali celo razvoj sladkorne bolezni tipa 2.
Torej vsa našteta dejstva o pomembnosti čim hitrejšega odkrivanja bolezni, kakor tudi preprečevanja zapletov diabetesa privedejo k temu, da je vsaj pri nekaterih, kjer obstaja še kakšen dejavnik tveganja, potrebno občasno izmeriti krvni sladkor.
Kdo se naj odloči za občasno, naključno kontrolo krvnega sladkorja?

Kakšne so normalne vrednosti in kdaj nastane sum za sladkorno bolezen?
- Normalna vrednost na tešče je 4,4-6,0 mmol/l, 2 uri po obroku pa 4,4-7,8 mmol/l
- Glukoza v krvi na tešče 7,0 mmol/l in 11 mmol/l kadarkoli pomeni postavitev diagnoze za sladkorno bolezen. (meritev mora biti opravljena vsaj dvakrat). Diagnozo postavi zdravnik.
Lekarniška zbornica,je že pred leti, pričela s tako imenovano Farmacevtsko skrbjo pri sladkorni bolezni, kamor se tudi v Lekarni Ormož sedaj pridružujemo. V lekarni nas torej lahko povprašate o razvoju bolezni, možnostih merjenja krvnega sladkorja tudi v lekarni, uporabi aparatov, ki jih že uporabljate in seveda o možnostih spremembe življenjskega sloga (prehranjevanje, gibanje), svetovanje glede nadaljnjih ukrepov glede na izmerjene vrednosti sladkorja v krvi(napotitev k zdravniku, ponovna kontrola v lekarni ali le svetovanje z nefarmakološkimi ukrepi (prehrana, gibanje).
