V stari kitajski praksi 'cepljenja' iz 10.stoletja so zaradi strahu pred črnimi kozami zdravim ljudem po ljudskem izročilu vpihovali v nos posušeno vsebino gnojnih kožnih razjed v prahu (posušene in zdrobljene kraste) kot preventiva pred boleznijo. Običaj je prvič uradno zabeležen v knjigi leta 1549 kitajskega avtorja Wan Quan. Okužba se je prišla v telo preko sluznice podobno kot pri naravni okužbi v stiku z obolelimi. Povzročila je bolj blago obliko bolezni z manjšo smrtnostjo.
INOKULACIJA
Okužba s starim kitajskim 'cepljenjem' z vpihavanjem v nos je imela smrtnost do 2%. Naravno pridobljena bolezen v stiku z obolelimi pa 20-30%. Zato so se zdravi ljudje kljub smrtnemu riziku prostovoljno izpostavljali tej praksi. V Evropi pa so okoli leta 1700 svežo vsebino gnojnih razjed obolelih z zarezami na roki že vnašali pod kožo zdravega človeka. Takšno 'cepljenje' se je imenovalo INOKULACIJA (tudi variolacija). Okužba ni potekala preko sluznice kot pri naravni okužbi v stiku z obolelimi temveč z vbrizgavanjem.
Tuberkoloza
Poleg 2% umrljivosti po 'cepljenju' z INOKULACIJO zaradi sproženega razvoja bolezni so imeli tudi mnogi preživeli resne stranske učinke kot reakcija telesa na kužne tujke. Nekateri pa so utrpeli tudi vseživljenjske posledice. V naslednjih letih pa so z INOKULACIJO 'cepljeno' prebivalstvo vedno bolj ogrožale tudi razne druge bolezni, predvsem tuberkoloza. Ta je postala vse bolj usodna predvsem za mnoge 'cepljene' ljudi, pri katerih je bil bolj pogost tudi sifilis in bakterijske okužbe šen (erysipel).
Edward Jenner 1796
Od tuberkoloze je umrl tudi sin angleškega zdravnika Edward Jennerja (1749-1823). Edward Jenner je pred 200 leti začel VAKCINACIJO kot prvo uradno metodo 'cepljenja' za črne koze in izdelal prvo 'moderno' cepivo ali VAKCINO. Zdelo se mu je, da ženske, ki so molzle bolne krave z razjedami po vimenu zaradi kravjih koz in so dobile po rokah tudi same takšne razjede zaradi stika pri molži, niso obolevale od črnih koz. Imele so lep obraz v nasprotju z večino deklet, ki so preživele črne koze in je bil njihov obraz izmaličen z brazgotinami.
VAKCINACIJA
Čeprav je bilo to daleč od dejanskega stanja in je mnogo ljudi obolevalo in tudi umrlo od črnih koz kljub temu da so prej preboleli kravje koze in jim to ni prineslo zaščite, se je Edward Jenner pred dobrimi 200 leti lotil dela. 14.maja 1796 je cepil 8-letnega dečka najprej z vsebino gnojnih razjed kravjih koz s svojim postopkom VAKCINACIJE. Vacca je krava, zato se prvo cepivo iz kravjih koz po njih imenuje vakcina. Čez mesec in pol pa je istega dečka še z vsebino gnojnih razjed črnih koz v več zarez na rokah z INOKULACIJO. Deček ni zbolel, kar je bilo zanj potrditev, da je na pravi poti.
Naravna imunost
V tistem času je bilo poleg množice bolnih tudi veliko imunih otrok in ljudi, ki niso zboleli za črnimi kozami kljub stiku z bolnimi. Ženske, ki so naravno prebolele in preživele bolezen, so rodile imune otroke. Za nekaj let so na otroke prenesle naravno imunost, tako da so bili zaščiteni v najnežnejših letih, vse dokler se ni izoblikoval njihov lastni imunski sistem. Imuni starši, ki so bolezen preživeli, so bili tudi živi zaščitni zid, da bolezen ni obiskala njihovih otrok in njihovega doma.
Test na ljudeh
Edward Jenner je preskočil raziskavo, ker tudi ni bil šolan zdravnik temveč le priučen na medicinski poklic skozi tedanja združenja, od 13.leta pa kot vajenec pri lekarnarju in znanem kirurgu. Članstvo v kraljevi družbi mu je prinesla študija kukavičjih mladičev. Direktno je cepil najprej samo tega 8-letnega dečka s kravjimi kozami s svojo VAKCINACIJO. Čez dober mesec pa ga je cepil še z INOKULACIJO s črnimi kozami in ker deček ni zbolel, si je to razložil kot uspeh.
Umrl pri 20-ih
Ta fant je kasneje pri 20-ih letih zbolel za hudo tuberkolozo in umrl. Za tuberkolozo je zbolela in umrla tudi žena Edwarda Jennerja, dve sestri in najstarejši sin, ki ga je kar dvakrat cepil potem ko je postopek VAKCINACIJE že nekoliko preizkusil. Leta 1798 pa je cepil še 5-letnega fantka z gnojem iz bolnih konjskih pet, osmi dan je bil še v redu, nato pa je umrl.
Novo upanje
Ker je bilo 'cepljenje' s pravimi črnimi kozami z INOKULACIJO zelo rizično in se je težko prenašalo, za mnoge pa se je hudo slabo končalo s trpljenjem v bolezni, so bili ljudje odprti novemu cepljenju VAKCINACIJE z bolj blagimi kravjimi kozami, ki naj bi ščitilo pred črnimi kozami. Še posebej ker je Edward Jenner obljubljal trajno in popolno doživljenjsko varnost tudi pred vsako ponovno okužbo pred črnimi kozami.
Podpora države
Tako je leta 1802 zaprosil za denar od parlamenta in 1807 prejel finančno podlago za masovno izdelavo cepiva oziroma VAKCINE. Kmalu se je izkazalo, da njegovo cepivo na osnovi kravjih koz ne varuje pred črnimi kozami, ker so mnogi cepljeni začeli obolevati in tudi umirati. Prizadeti cepljeni so se pritoževali, oblasti pa so skupaj z Edward Jennerjem stalno našle razloge zakaj cepivo ni učinkovito. Ker cepljenje ni dovolj pogosto, da odmerki niso pravi, število vbodov je premalo, surovina ni dovolj čista.
Izgovori
Poslužili so se preimenovanja bolezni z izgovorom, da cepljeni niso umrli od črnih koz, temveč od 'lažnih kravjih koz'. Smrti cepljenih zaradi črnih koz so v bolnišnicah pripisali 'postularnemu ekcemu'. Tako da se je praksa cepljenja na osnovi kravjih koz še kar nadaljevala kljub temu da več kot očitno ni preprečila črnih koz. Edward Jenner je leta 1823 umrl za že drugo kapjo.
Zakonsko obvezno od 1853
30 let kasneje je leta 1853 je postalo njegovo cepljenje proti črnim kozam z VAKCINACIJO obvezno z zakonom. Po samo treh letih pa so v Angliji pustošile tri dveletne epidemije: leta 1857, 1863 in 1870. Kljub polni precepljenosti prebivalstva je bila vsaka hujša od naslednje. V prvi je bilo 14 tisoč smrti zaradi črnih koz, v drugi 20 tisoč in v tretji 45 tisoč.
Najhujše epidemije
Drugače povedano je bilo v prvih desetih letih od 1853 po uvedbi obveznega cepljenja z VAKCINACIJO v Veliki Britaniji 33 tisoč smrti, v drugih desetih letih pa 70 tisoč. Leta 1907 je bil zakon o obveznem cepljenju razveljavljen. Anglija in Wales sta do leta 1919 postali eni od najmanj cepljenih dežel in sta imeli samo še 28 smrti na 38 milijonov prebivalcev.
Filipini
Na Filipinih pa so od leta 1905 Združene Države Amerike večkrat prisilno izvajale cepilne kampanje. Ko je bilo leta 1918 cepljeno že prek 95% filipinskega prebivalstva, je Filipine napadla najhujša epidemija črnih koz, ki je bila veliko hujša od vseh dotedanjih in bolj usodna. Na področjih, kjer je bila smrtnost 10-15%, je bila tedaj 60%, to je kar dvakrat višja od povprečja.
Iztrebljene 1980
Črne koze so bile v Evropi najpogostejši vzrok smrti zaradi bolezni. 5% preživelih je bilo slepih zaradi uničene roženice ali pa so imeli poškodbe udov zaradi artritisa in osteomelitisa. V 20. stoletju so črne koze odnesle v Evropi 300-500 milijonov življenj. Leta 1980 je bolezen črnih koz razglašena kot prva bolezen, ki je iztrebljena. Druga iztrebljena pa je Sars-Cov, visoko smrtna 'kamelja gripa' na bližnjem vzhodu.
Dr. Hadwen
Zakulisje cepljenja je bilo že na samem začetku zelo turbulentno. Več stoletij razširjanja črnih koz z INOKULACIJO in VAKCINACIJO zaradi strahu pred boleznijo in s tem rizičnemu izpostavljanju zdravih ljudi je zahtevalo stotisoče smrti. Cepljeni pa so bili v prvih dveh tednih kužni in so še prispevali k razširjanju teh strašnih epidemij. Leta 1986 je dr. Hadwen izjavil, da je Edward Jenner genialno odkril, da je bolj donosno prodati cepivo vsem naivnim in prestrašenim, ki ga lahko kupijo, kot pa zdraviti peščico bolnih, ki si ne more plačati zdravljenja.
Dr. Ana Gligič
Leta 1972 je beograjska virologinja dr. Ana Gligič z mednarodnim slovesom vodila skupino strokovnjakov, ki so izolirali virus črnih koz, ki se je s 175 obolelimi in 35 umrlimi pojavil tudi v tedanji Jugoslaviji. Romar iz Kosova je na poti iz Meke v Iraku kupil piščal od trgovca z značilno gnojno razjedo na licu.
V Jugoslaviji
Pred odhodom v Meko je bil romar cepljen proti črnim kozam in sam ob povratku ni zbolel. Črne koze pa so se na Kosovu in v Srbiji vseeno pojavile. Serološka preiskava je pri romarju odkrila okužbo, ki jo je ob tem da je bil cepljen, po vrnitvi prenašal na svojce. Bolezen se je v enem mesecu razširila na 18 naselij na Kosovu in v 8 naselij v Srbiji.
Februar 1972
Strogo karanteno so odredili za 10 tisoč ljudi, ki so bili v stiku. V nekaj dnevih pa so v celotni Jugoslaviji izvedli množično izredno cepljenje okoli 20 milijonov ljudi. V Sloveniji je bilo v desetih dneh cepljeno milijon in pol ljudi, kar je bilo 86% tedanjega prebivalstva. Sredi aprila 1972 je bil razglašen konec nevarnosti. Velike zasluge ima pri zaustavitvi črnih koz v Jugoslaviji ugledna virologinja dr. Ana Gligič.
Napoved koronavirus
Sedaj je dr. Gligič že upokojena, v izjavi glede koronavirusa pa je za beograjsko televizijo N1 povedala, da je koronavirus oslabel. Napoveduje, da ne bo drugega vala razen kakšnih lokalnih žarišč. Ta pa bodo z že utečenimi preventivnimi ukrepi kmalu izzvenela. Iz svojih bogatih izkušenj kot virologinja je letos marca 2020 sredi najhujše pandemije pravilno sklepala glede na dotlej ugotovljena dejstva koronavirusa. V intervjuju za javnost je izjavila, da bomo maja 2020 že pili kavico na terasah lokalov in še kako res je.

Knowledge for Better Health
Safe Food While Traveling - Recommendations for Travelers
A risk factor for traveler's diarrhea depends on the area you are traveling to. The incidence rate is higher for travelers from developed countries who travel to less developed countries, and it is around 50%.
Classification of areas according to the risk level for traveler's diarrhea:
- low-risk areas (up to 7% probability of traveler's diarrhea): USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Northern and Western Europe.
- medium-risk areas (8–20%): Eastern Europe, South Africa, and some Caribbean islands.
- high-risk areas (20–50%): most of Asia, Central and South America, parts of the Middle East, and Africa.
Risky foods:
- food served at room temperature
- food that has not been heat-treated
- unpeeled vegetables and fruits (tomatoes, strawberries, grapes, etc.)
- salads and other raw vegetables
- unpasteurized milk and dairy products
- tap water, ice cubes
- street food, ice cream
- cream-based desserts
- salad dressings, cold appetizers
- seafood (shellfish, crabs)
- spices and condiments in open containers
Transmission of infection
Infection usually occurs by consuming contaminated food and liquids, but the pathogen can also be transmitted to the body through your hands. Bacteria are the predominant cause, accounting for 80-90% of cases of traveler's diarrhea. The pathogen is excreted in the stool of the infected person for a certain period. The excretion of the pathogen usually does not stop when the patient recovers, but continues in the stool for several weeks or months. From the patient or carrier, the pathogen returns to the environment, where, in unsanitary conditions (inadequate access to drinking water, inadequate sewage and waste disposal), the infection can more easily spread to healthy individuals.
Course of infection
It is usually a mild form of diarrhea that resolves on its own within a few days. If it is accompanied by a high body temperature or if there is blood in the stool, medical attention is needed. In the case of traveler's diarrhea, ensure adequate replacement of lost fluids and electrolytes. The best option is to use pre-prepared rehydration powders and solutions. In more severe cases, medications that slow down bowel movements and certain specific medications can be used to treat traveler's diarrhea, but these must be prescribed by a doctor.
Vulnerable groups
Traveler's diarrhea is particularly dangerous for infants and young children, pregnant women, the elderly, and people with weakened immune systems due to the risk of dehydration.
Prevention of traveler's diarrhea
The most important thing in preventing traveler's diarrhea is to follow general hygiene measures and to carefully choose food and drink bottled beverages. Hand hygiene is an important way to prevent infection. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and clean water as often as possible, before each meal and after using the toilet. If drinking water is not available, we recommend using wet wipes or alcohol-based hand sanitizers.
|A general rule for choosing food while traveling is: COOK, PEEL, or FORGET IT!|
Safe food and drinks
- freshly prepared and adequately heat-treated food, kept at a temperature above 63°C until consumed, and cold dishes, kept at a temperature below 4°C
- pre-packaged dry food (bread, crackers)
- very sweet food (syrup, jam)
- peeled vegetables and fruits
- fresh vegetables and fruits that you clean and peel yourself
- bottled beverages (originally sealed)

Varna hrana na potovanju - priporočila potnikom
Dejavnik tveganja za potovalno drisko je odvisen od področja, kamor potujemo. Stopnja obolevnosti je večja pri popotnikih, ki iz razvitega sveta potujejo v manj razvite države in znaša okrog 50 %.
Razdelitev področij glede na stopnjo tveganja za potovalno drisko:
- območja z nizkim tveganjem (do 7 % verjetnosti za pojav potovalne driske): ZDA, Kanada, Avstralija, Nova Zelandija, Japonska, Severna in Zahodna Evropa.
- območja s srednjim tveganjem (8–20 %): Vzhodna Evropa, Južna Afrika in nekateri otoki Karibskega otočja.
- območja z visokim tveganjem (20–50 %): večji del Azije, Srednja in Južna Amerika, deli Srednjega vzhoda in Afrika.
Tvegana živila:

- hrana, ki ni toplotno obdelana
- neolupljena zelenjava in sadje (paradižnik, jagode, grozdje itd.)

Do okužbe običajno pride ob uživanju onesnažene hrane in tekočin, lahko pa povzročitelja prenesemo v telo tudi preko svojih rok. Med povzročitelji prevladujejo bakterije, ki so vzrok za 80-90 % potovalnih drisk. Povzročitelj se določen čas izloča z blatom obolelega. Izločanje klic praviloma ne preneha, ko bolnik okreva, ampak izločanje z blatom traja še nekaj tednov ali mesecev. Z bolnika ali klicenosca se povzročitelj vrača v okolje, kjer se v higiensko neurejenih razmerah (neustrezna oskrba s pitno vodo, neurejeno odvajanje odplak in odpadkov) okužba lažje širi na zdrave posameznike.

Običajno gre za blago obliko driske, ki mine sama od sebe v nekaj dneh. Kadar jo spremlja povišana telesna temperatura ali pa je blatu primešana kri, je potrebna zdravniška pomoč. V primeru pojava potovalne driske poskrbimo za ustrezno nadomeščanje izgubljene tekočine in elektrolitov. Najbolj primerna je uporaba že pripravljenih rehidracijskih praškov in raztopin. V težjih primerih lahko za zdravljenje potovalne driske uporabljamo tudi pripravke, ki upočasnijo praznjenje črevesja in določena specifična zdravila, ki pa jih mora predpisati zdravnik.

Potovalna driska je še posebej nevarna za dojenčke in majhne otroke, nosečnice, starejše osebe in osebe z zmanjšano odpornostjo zaradi nevarnosti izsušitve organizma oziroma dehidracije.

Pri preprečevanju potovalne driske je najpomembnejše upoštevanje splošnih higienskih ukrepov ter skrbna izbira hrane in uživanje ustekleničenih pijač. Higiena rok predstavlja pomemben način preprečevanja okužbe. Roke si čim pogosteje temeljito umivamo z milom in čisto vodo, pred vsako jedjo in po uporabi stranišča. V kolikor pitna voda ni dosegljiva, svetujemo uporabo mokrih higienskih oziroma alkoholnih robčkov.

Fever – Elevated Body Temperature
Fever is a condition characterized by an elevated body temperature. It is a common and non-specific symptom. The normal body temperature is around 36.2–37.2°C, but there can be significant variations between individuals. It also depends on age, gender, diet, physical activity, menstrual cycle, etc. Generally, it is highest in the evening and lowest in the morning. Fever is defined as a temperature above 37°C under the arm (or 37.8°C when measured under the tongue, 37.5°C in the ear, and 38°C rectally). An increase in body temperature above 38°C is called febrile temperature, while a temperature below 38°C is called subfebrile temperature.

How does fever occur?
Body temperature is regulated by the thermoregulatory center in the brain (hypothalamus), which functions similarly to a thermostat. An increase in the set point (thermostat) is directly caused by PGE2, which is released when pyrogens (substances that cause fever) are present in the body. Pyrogens can be endogenous, meaning they are produced within the body, or exogenous, meaning they enter the body from the environment. The most common cause of fever is infection with microorganisms such as viruses and bacteria. Fever can also be caused by various allergens, insect bites, sunburn, tumors, and side effects of medications.

When is fever not dangerous?
The general consensus is that any fever is dangerous because it harms the body. However, this is not entirely true. Fever is an important defense mechanism of the body and an ally in the fight against disease. Elevated body temperature prevents and stops the reproduction of microorganisms that cause the disease. High temperature reduces their activity and harmfulness. Fever also stimulates the body's immune system, increasing the effectiveness of killer cells (T lymphocytes) that fight microbes. This is especially important in all viral diseases that cannot be treated with antibiotics.

A fever up to 38.5°C (measured under the arm) helps the body's defense mechanisms, so it should not be reduced, except in cases where it causes significant discomfort. Exceptions are children with heart and chronic lung diseases, febrile seizures, diabetes, and epilepsy. Fever plays a defensive role by stimulating defense factors and contributing to faster recovery.

When is fever dangerous?
Fever is dangerous for people with heart conditions. An increase in body temperature of 1°C increases the heart rate by 15 to 20 beats per minute, which puts additional strain on the heart. Seek medical attention when the temperature rises above 40 degrees or if febrile seizures, stiff neck, difficulty breathing with blue lips, refusal to drink fluids, if the child is small, if the fever lasts more than three days, if bloody red rashes appear, in case of dehydration, or if other symptoms of the disease are present along with the fever.

Kako do vročine pride?
Telesno temperaturo nadzira termoregulacijski center v možganih (hipotalamus), ki se obnaša zelo podobno kot termostat. Splošno sprejeto mnenje je, da je vsaka vročina nevarna, ker škoduje organizmu. Vendar to ne drži. Vročina je zelo pomemben obrambni mehanizem telesa in bolnikov zaveznik v boju proti bolezni. Vročina tudi spodbuja delovanje obrambnega sistema telesa, poveča se učinkovitost celic ubijalk (Limfocit T), ki se bojujejo z mikrobi. Nuts, legumes, and seeds contain toxic substances and anti-nutrients in their outer layers, which allow them to survive in nature until favorable conditions for their growth appear. When enough rain falls, these substances are washed away from the surface of the nuts, allowing them to germinate. When we soak nuts, we are essentially mimicking the processes that occur in nature. The outer layers of nuts, seeds, and legumes contain a significant amount of toxic substances, such as: ACE, phytates, goitrogens, and enzyme inhibitors.

The problem with phytic acid is that it can bind to iron, magnesium, zinc, copper, and calcium in the digestive tract, which significantly reduces the absorption of these substances into the bloodstream. The consequences manifest as irritable bowel syndrome, osteoporosis due to bone mass loss, and mineral deficiencies. It is important to remember that soaking nuts in warm water for several hours removes or neutralizes phytic acid. Enzyme inhibitors, which are also found in the outer layers of nuts, seeds, and legumes, inhibit and prevent the function of metabolic and digestive enzymes. This can cause significant harm to our digestion and metabolism.

The outer layers of nuts, seeds, and legumes also contain a lot of tannins, which, if consumed in large quantities, interfere with the absorption of minerals (zinc, magnesium, and copper), as well as iron and calcium. ACEs are growth inhibitors that are also found in the shells of nuts. There is undeniable evidence that ACEs cause fatigue, headaches, inflammation, pain, and dry cough. It is especially recommended that pregnant women avoid them. Goitrogenic substances are also found among the harmful compounds in the outer layers of nuts, seeds, and legumes. These are natural substances that inhibit the normal function of the thyroid gland by interfering with iodine uptake.

Therefore, nuts, seeds, and legumes must be soaked in warm water for several hours before use. It is best to do this overnight. We apply this principle whether we are cooking a bean stew or preparing a handful of our favorite nuts for a snack.

Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

A child develops their speech by listening to and imitating the speech of adults. How early and how fluently they will speak depends primarily on the child themselves. Individual children from the same linguistic environment can develop very differently. The main task of parents is to accept the child as an equal speaker: listen when they speak, show interest, and don't interrupt. It is also important to limit the use of a pacifier to bedtime after the child's first birthday. Excessive use of a pacifier during the day, among other things, prevents play with speech organs.

The main task of parents is to accept the child as an equal speaker: listen when they speak, show interest, and don't interrupt.
Don't correct the child, but help them distinguish between correctly and incorrectly pronounced words.
When a child speaks fluently, they usually make many mistakes in their speech. It is important not to point these out or correct them. A clear and distinct repetition will suffice: "There's a goat among the rocks!" "Did you find a crab among the rocks?"
It is better to teach the child to distinguish between correctly and incorrectly pronounced words than to correct them. This can be done through play:
Open the thumb and index finger in a clenched fist and ask the child: "Which is correct: 'sebela' (show the thumb) or 'chebela' (show the index finger)?" The child then points to the finger they believe the word was pronounced correctly with. Always focus on a single sound that the child is having trouble with (e.g., sebela/chebela or chebeya/chebela).
It is better to teach the child to distinguish between correctly and incorrectly pronounced words than to correct them.
Exercises for individual sounds
The pronunciation of the L sound is usually developed by the age of four, the R sound between the ages of four and five, the C, S, and Z sounds by the age of five, and the CH, SH, and ZH sounds by the age of six. You can start with the simplest exercises to loosen the tongue, which I wrote about in the first part of the article, even with a baby. These exercises are then gradually expanded and later used in words. First with a pause, then fluently: sss_lon, ssslon; no_sss, nosss; go_sss_pa, gossspa.
⇒L sound: chattering (~~~, the tip of the tongue quickly moves up and down on the upper teeth).
⇒Sibilants (C, S, Z): imitating a snake (sss), a mouse (ts, ts, ts), and a bee (zzz). In these exercises, the tongue should be "locked," hidden behind the lower teeth.
⇒Fricatives (CH, SH, ZH): imitating the wind (shsh), a train (ch, ch, ch), and a saw (zhzh). In these exercises, the tongue is also "locked," this time behind the upper teeth, and the lips are rounded.
⇒R sound: singing melodies on da-da-da or ta-da-dan. Choose those that are often sung in the family. First, perform the exercise slowly, then gradually, always faster, while the sounds t and d must be clearly pronounced – on the hard palate behind the upper teeth. (Depending on the speed of execution, you could first choose a few bars of the song Smoke on the Water by Deep Purple, then the theme from the movie Topgun, Avsenik's Na golici, and finally, for masters, the melody from Rossini's opera Guillaume Tell). Of course, you can also stick to Kuža pazi and Zajček dolgoušček.
You can find a variety of useful tips and video demonstrations of learning to pronounce individual sounds on the Gingo talk website, which promotes speech and language. A book, which uses stories to provide exercises for individual sounds, can also be a great tool for dealing with pronunciation problems.

A speech therapist should help with systematic learning
The exercises described above have proven to be most effective in the youngest members of our family, especially in the form of short speech therapy games during the hectic everyday life. I like to use moments for language skills training when it comes to everyday communication in the family: "Mommy, can I have a t-shirt?" I am surprised: "T-shirt?" and I tug at the child's clothes. Because they are used to language jokes, they immediately know what it is about. We quickly do the chattering exercise and incorporate it into the word: "~~~, ma_~~~_co, malllco." I praise them, even if the exercise doesn't go very well. At that moment, the example of correct execution and the child's empty stomach are most important.
For a four-year-old who has been playing with sound games since they started babbling, the method described above may work. However, a more systematic approach is needed for an older child who has never done such exercises. A speech therapist can teach the child the correct execution of the exercise in a personal meeting. There is a risk that we teach the child certain movements incorrectly – what is learned incorrectly is much more difficult to correct than something that has not been learned at all.
Speech irregularities that can be relatively easily corrected are only a small part of a speech therapist's work. A more important area of speech therapy is language and communication disorders, which can affect the quality of life even in adulthood. You can read about what a child is capable of at a certain age and when it is really important to seek help from a speech therapist here.
Let's not forget the home language
When we encourage a child to speak understandably, we often overuse formal language. However, the family's colloquial language is the child's first native language. We can be proud of dialects, as they define an individual's identity and enrich us. If we speak in our native language at home, the child will not have language problems, experts say. The child will learn the differences between language styles over time by observing adults, through reading books, and later in school. Therefore, let's be brave and incorporate language exercises into the dialect.

Otrok razvija svoj govor ob poslušanju in s posnemanjem govora odraslih. Kako zgodaj in kako gostobesedno bo spregovoril, je odvisno predvsem od njega samega. Posamezni otroci iz istega govornega okolja se lahko razvijajo zelo različno. Naloga staršev je predvsem ta, da sprejmemo otroka za enakovrednega govorca: poslušamo, ko govori, pokažemo zanimanje in ne skačemo v besedo. Pomembno je tudi to, da po prvem letu otrokove starosti omejimo uporabo dude na čas za spanje. Pretirana uporaba dude čez dan med drugim namreč preprečuje igro z govorili.

Ko otrok tekoče spregovori, običajno v svojem govoru, dela celo vrsto napak. Pomembno je, da ga na té ne opozarjamo in ga ne popravljamo. Zadostovala bo jasna in razločna ponovitev: »Med skajami je jakec!« »Med skalami si našel rakca?«
Otroka raje, kot da ga popravljamo, učimo razlikovanja med pravilno in napačno izgovorjenimi besedami. To lahko storimo z igro:
V stisnjeni pesti odpremo palec in kazalec in otroka vprašamo: »Kako je prav: sebela (pokažem palec) ali čebela (pokažem kazalec)?« Otrok nato pokaže tisti prst, za katerega meni, da je bila beseda izgovorjena pravilno. Vedno se osredotočimo na en sam glas, ki otroku dela težave (npr. sebela/čebela ali čebeja/čebela).

Vaje za posamezne glasove
Izgovarjavo glasu L otrok praviloma razvije do četrtega leta, glas R med četrtim in petim letom, glasove C, S, Z do petega, Č, Š, Ž pa do šestega leta. Z najbolj enostavnimi vajami za razgibavanje jezika, o katerih sem pisala v prvem delu prispevka, lahko začnemo že pri dojenčku. Te vaje nato postopoma nadgrajujemo ter jih pozneje uporabimo tudi v besedah. Najprej s premorom, nato tekoče: sss_lon, ssslon; no_sss, nosss; go_sss_pa, gossspa.
⇒Glas L: klepetulja (~~~, konica jezika opleta po gornjih zobeh hitro ven in noter),
⇒Sičniki (C, S, Z): oponašanje kače (sss), miške (ts, ts, ts) in čebele (zzz). Pri teh vajah mora biti jezik »v zaporu«, skrit za spodnjimi zobmi.
⇒Šumniki (Č, Š, Ž): oponašanje vetra (ššš), vlaka (č, č, č) in žage (žžž). Tudi pri teh vajah je jezik »v zaporu«, tokrat za zgornjimi zobmi, ustnice pa so našobljene.
⇒Glas R: petje melodij na da-da-da ali ta-da-dan. Izberemo tiste, ki si jih v družini pogosto popevamo. Vajo najprej izvajamo počasi, nato postopoma, vedno hitreje, pri čemer morata biti jasno izgovorjena glasova t in d – na trdem nebu za zgornjimi zobmi. (Glede na hitrost izvedbe bi lahko najprej izbrali nekaj taktov skladbe Smoke on the water skupine Deep Purple, nato temo iz filma Topgun, Avsenikovo Na golici in nazadnje, za mojstre, melodijo iz Rossinijeve opere Guillaume Tell). Lahko pa seveda ostanete tudi pri Kuža pazi in Zajček dolgoušček.
Vrsto koristnih nasvetov in video prikazov učenja izgovarjave posameznih glasov vam je na voljo na spletišču za spodbujanje govora in jezika Gingo talk. Odličen pripomoček pri težavah z izgovorjavo je lahko tudi knjiga, s pomočjo katere preko zgodb delamo vaje za posamezne glasove.
Pri sistematičnem učenju naj pomaga logoped
Zgoraj opisane vaje so se pri najmlajših članih naše družine izkazale za najbolj učinkovite predvsem v obliki kratkih logopedskih iger med norim vsakdanjikom. Za urjenje jezikovnih spretnosti namreč rada izkoristim trenutke, ko gre za sprotno komunikacijo v družini: »Mami, a daš maj’co?« Začudim se: »Majco?« in pocukam otrokovo oblačilo. Ker je vajen jezikovnih šal, takoj ve, za kaj gre. Hitro narediva vajo klepetulje in jo vpleteva v besedo: »~~~, ma_~~~_co, malllco«. Pohvalim ga, četudi mu vaja ne uspe najbolje. V tistem trenutku je pomemben predvsem zgled pravilne izvedbe in otrokov prazen želodček.
Pri štiriletniku, ki se srečuje z glasovnimi igricami, odkar je začel čebljati, bo zgoraj opisani način lahko deloval. K starejšemu otroku, ki še nikoli ni izvajal takšnih vaj, pa bo treba pristopiti bolj sistematično. Pravilno izvedbo vaje bo otroka lahko naučil samo logoped na osebnem srečanju. Obstaja namreč nevarnost, da otroka določene gibe naučimo narobe – kar je narobe naučeno, pa je mnogo teže popraviti kot nekaj, kar sploh še ni naučeno.
Glasovne nepravilnosti, ki jih je sorazmerno lahko odpraviti, so le majhen del logopedovega dela. Pomembnejše področje logopedije so jezikovne in komunikacijske motnje, ki lahko vplivajo na kakovost življenja tudi v dobi odraslosti. O tem, kaj vse otrok pri določeni starosti zmore in kdaj je zares pomembno poiskati pomoč logopeda, si lahko preberete tukaj.
Ne pozabimo na domačo govorico
Kadar otroka spodbujamo k razumljivemu govoru, se rado zgodi, da pretirano uporabljamo knjižni jezik. A prav pogovorni jezik družine je otrokov prvi materni jezik. Na narečja smo lahko ponosni, saj opredeljujejo posameznikovo pripadnost in nas bogatijo. Če bomo v družini govorili po domače, otrok zaradi tega ne bo imel jezikovnih težav, menijo strokovnjaki. Razlikovanja med jezikovnimi zvrstmi se bo otrok sčasoma naučil ob zgledu odraslih, preko branja knjig in pozneje v šoli. Zato le pogumno, jezikovne vaje lahko vpletemo tudi v narečno govorico.

BACKGROUND. Water is a medium that makes up a significant portion of the body. The balance of water and electrolytes is a crucial mechanism for maintaining homeostasis and proper functioning of bodily processes. A key hormone responsible for regulating water balance is arginine vasopressin, which is synthesized in the brain – in the hypothalamus – and stored in the pituitary gland. The stimulus for its release is a lack of water in the body. When this balance is disrupted, certain clinical conditions arise. This article covers the basic pathophysiological mechanisms, causes, symptoms, and clinical signs of these conditions. I have focused in more detail on water intoxication during sports. Recommendations for proper and balanced hydration for athletes during physical activity are also provided.

1. INTRODUCTION
Water makes up 45-60% of a person's body weight, depending on age. Understanding its distribution in the body is crucial for understanding the mechanisms of water and salt deficiency. Water is distributed between the intracellular space (ICS) and the extracellular space (ECS). 3/5 of the water is in the ICS and 2/5 in the ECS. The water in the ECS is distributed between the interstitial fluid and plasma in a 3:1 ratio (Figure 1). Water movement depends on the osmolality of the compartments, i.e., the concentration of electrolytes in each compartment. Among the electrolytes, Na+ is the most important, and it is primarily ingested in the form of salt. The body loses water through the skin via sweating and diffusion, through urine, from the digestive tract via vomiting and stool, and through the respiratory system via diffusion. In a healthy person, the balance of water and sodium is zero, meaning they are in equilibrium. The kidneys are the main organ that maintains this zero balance. The main stimulus for adequate water intake is thirst, and numerous physiological mechanisms are involved in water excretion (the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, natriuretic hormone, sympathetic innervation of renal arterioles, and urodilantin). In this article, we will review the basic mechanisms of water and electrolyte balance and focus on how this balance changes during exercise and what the body's response is to exercise based on the water content in the body.
Figure 1. Distribution of water in the main compartments of the human body.
2. HYPERHYDRATION
Hyperhydration is a condition of increased water in the body, resulting from a positive balance of water and Na+. It occurs due to increased intake and/or decreased excretion of water and salt (Na+) through the kidneys. A common characteristic of all hyperhydration conditions is an increased volume of the ECS, due to water. The total amount of Na+ in the ECS may be increased or normal.
There are 3 types of hyperhydration, depending on the redistribution of the solute (salt):
- Isotonic hyperhydration: is the result of a positive balance of water and salt. The causes of this condition can be excessive intake of isotonic fluid in a healthy person or excessive intake of water and salt in patients with chronic kidney disease, where the kidneys are too damaged to correct this condition.
- Hypertonic hyperhydration: is the result of a positive balance of water and salt, where the intake of salt is greater than the intake of water. This is characterized by an increased concentration of Na+ in the plasma and an increased amount of water in the ECS. The cause can be an overdose of corticosteroids, Na+ poisoning, and various clinical diseases (Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, etc.).
- Hypotonic hyperhydration: is the result of a positive balance of water and salt, where the concentration of salt is lower than the volume of water. The concentration of Na+ is lower in the plasma, and the volume of the ECS is increased due to water. Clinical diseases that cause this condition are chronic heart failure, chronic liver diseases, and nephrotic syndrome.
3. DEHYDRATION
Dehydration is a condition in which there is a lack of water in the body, resulting from a negative balance of water and salt. This is a state of "drying out," where loss is greater than intake. This condition can lead to hypovolemia – a decrease in blood pressure in the veins, which can cause impaired consciousness, general weakness, and helplessness. Mechanisms are activated to correct and maintain this state, which people experience as a strong and sudden feeling of thirst, oliguria – minimal urine output, tachycardia – an increased heart rate, and an acute decrease in body weight.
Dehydration also involves 3 pathophysiological principles:
- Isotonic dehydration: is the result of a negative balance of water and salt, where the loss is in the same ratio. Clinical conditions that lead to this are diarrhea, acute external bleeding, and acute kidney failure.
- Hypertonic dehydration: is the result of a negative balance of water and salt, where the loss of water is greater than the loss of salt. In this case, the person loses water from the ECS and ICS, and salt from the ECS. A condition that leads to this is profuse sweating, especially during physical activity, where lost water and salt are not replaced. It can also be a state of inability to drink water, for example, in cases of unconsciousness, mental impairment, or in children and infants.
- Hypotonic dehydration: is the result of a negative balance of water and salt, where the loss of salt is greater than the loss of water. The person loses water from the ECS into the urine. This reduces the volume of blood due to the loss of water. This condition can occur when an athlete replaces lost fluid only with water, without electrolytes (without salt), or in patients with Addison's disease (who do not have the hormones aldosterone and cortisol).
4. HYPONATREMIA AND WATER INTOXICATION IN SPORTS
Hyponatremia describes a condition of lower than normal concentration of Na+ in the blood (135 - 145 mmol/l) and is the most common electrolyte disorder that can lead to water intoxication during hyperhydration. As mentioned earlier, Na+ is a key electrolyte and prevents water from entering cells. In the case of hyponatremia, water enters the cells and they swell. The key hormone responsible for regulating water balance in the body is AVP. It is released from the brain – from the hypothalamus – in response to a decreased volume in the ECS. Impaired release from the hypothalamus can occur due to neuropsychiatric disorders, infections, injuries, and bleeding in the brain. Common causes of this condition are also drugs that cause hyponatremia through various mechanisms.
In sports, this occurs due to excessive drinking of hypotonic fluids during intense physical exertion (such as a marathon). This is called exercise-associated hyponatremia (EAH). This is an acute condition with a decrease in the concentration of sodium ions in the blood below 135 mmol/l. Risk factors for this are low body mass, poor fitness, running for more than four hours, high environmental temperatures, and frequent fluid intake during running.
4.1. Mechanism of exercise-associated hyponatremia
The primary mechanism of EAH is excessive intake of hypotonic fluids such as water and various sports drinks, combined with decreased secretion of water in the distal tubule of the kidneys due to the release of arginine vasopressin (AVP). This is mainly seen in slower marathon runners.
AVP hormone is usually inhibited by lower plasma salt concentration. In some athletes, this does not happen, which can be observed with inappropriately high osmolality of urine – very concentrated urine. Stimuli for the release of AVP can be pain, emotions, physical exertion, nausea, vomiting, hypoglycemia, exposure to heat, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, etc.
The loss of sodium with sweat varies greatly among individuals. Increased sweating can lead to the development of hyponatremia due to the loss of salt, increased release of AVP, and intake of fluids that are more hypotonic than sweat. A large amount of osmotically inactive sodium in the body is located in the bones, skin, and cartilage and can potentially be converted into an osmotically active form. EAH may be a consequence of the inability to convert sodium into an active form.
4.2. Symptoms during physical exertion
As the concentration of sodium in the blood decreases, water moves into the cells. Symptomatic hyponatremia is most often manifested by neurological dysfunction. The brain is most affected, as it cannot expand due to the limited space in the skull. This increases intracranial pressure and reduces cerebral blood flow, which initially manifests as headache, impaired coordination, nausea, vomiting, and muscle cramps. Confusion and impaired consciousness occur. Later, coma and respiratory arrest occur due to compression of the brainstem.
Because the symptoms of hyponatremia are similar to those that occur with dehydration, it is important to assess the degree of hydration, which is better reflected in athletes by determining the osmolality (concentration) of urine and its specific gravity than by determining the osmolality of the blood. In practice, a bathroom test is used, where acute loss of body mass due to loss of body fluids is measured during exercise.
5. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR WATER AND ELECTROLYTE INTAKE DURING EXERCISE
Drinking diluted glucose-electrolyte solutions is an effective way to prevent dehydration and has a positive effect on physical performance. The need for water and electrolytes during physical exertion depends on the individual, the environment, the intensity, and the duration of the exertion. The athlete should be well-hydrated before starting exercise, with normal electrolyte levels in the plasma. Fluid intake during exercise should match the losses due to sweating and urination. During exercise, the athlete should reduce dehydration so that the loss of body weight is no more than 2%. For optimal rehydration, it is necessary to drink 1.5 liters of fluid for every kilogram of body weight lost. The athlete should drink slowly, in small amounts, every 15 minutes. The drink should contain 5 to 10 percent carbohydrates, 20 to 30 mmol/l of sodium, and 2 to 5 mmol/l of potassium. The addition of sodium is recommended for exercises lasting longer than 2 hours or for exercises where sodium losses in sweat are high.
6. CONCLUSION
Homeostatic balance of fluids in the body is important for the healthy functioning of the organism. Every cell in our body needs water to function, which plays an important role in regulating body temperature, transporting nutrients, and removing waste products. The amount of water that needs to be ingested into the body depends on the climatic conditions and physical activity. It is important to be aware of the proper use of electrolyte drinks in combination with water. It is necessary to adjust it according to the intensity of sports activity, according to physical endurance and constitution, and to replenish all lost substances in the body.
7. REFERENCES

- Dr. Axe, food is medicine: Water intoxication: How much water is too much? [cited 2018 April 8]. Available at: https://draxe.com/water-intoxication/
- Fry AC, and K Farrington. “Management of Acute Renal Failure.” Postgraduate Medical Journal 82.964 (2006): 106–116. PMC. Web. 6 Apr. 2018.
- Hew-Butler T, Loi V, Pani A, Rosner MH. Exercise Associated Hyponatremia: 2017 Update. Front. Med. 2017; 4 (21): 1–10.
- Hlastan Ribič C. Nutrition in top sports: a textbook for students of medicine and dentistry. Ljubljana: Medical Faculty; 2010.
- Košnik M.[et al.]. Internal medicine. Ljubljana: Littera Picta, Slovenian Medical Society; 2011.
- Okorn H. Needs for water and electrolytes during exercise. Sports Medicine. 2015; 1. p. 42–46.
- Ribarič S. Seminars in pathological physiology. Ljubljana: Medical Faculty, Institute for Pathological Physiology; 2014.
- Rotovnik Kozjek N. Clinical sports nutrition: from theory to practice. Med Razgl. 2014; 53 (4): 555–64.
Author of the article: Mateja Zidarič, a student of medicine at the Medical Faculty of Ljubljana; published on September 28, 2018.

IZHODIŠČA. Voda je medij, ki predstavlja velik delež v telesu. Ravnovesje vode in elektrolitov je ključen mehanizem za uravnano homeostazo in pravilno delovanje procesov v telesu. Ključen hormon odgovoren za uravnavanje ravnovesja vode je hormon arginin vazopresin, ki se sintetizira v možganih – v hipotalamusu in se shranjuje v hipofizi. Stimulus za njegovo izločanje je pomankanje vode v telesu. Ob porušenem ravnovesju nastopijo določena klinična stanja. V članku so zajeti osnovni patofiziološki mehanizmi nastopa določenih stanj, vzroki, simptomi in klinični znaki. Podrobneje sem se osredotočila na zastrupitev z vodo med športnimi napori. Opisana pa so tudi priporočila za pravilno in uravnoteženo hidracijo športnikov med telesno aktivnostjo.
1. UVOD
Voda v človeškem telesu predstavlja 45-60% telesne teže in je odvisna od starosti. Izrednega pomena je razumevanje njene porazdelitve v telesu, da lahko razumemo spodaj naštete mehanizme pomankanja vode in soli. Voda je porazdeljena med znotrajceličnim prostorom (ZNCP) in zunajceličnim prostorom (ZUCP). Kar 3/5 vode se nahaja v ZNCP in 2/5 v ZUCP. Pri čemer je voda v ZUCP razporejena med intersticijsko tekočino in plazmo v ramerju 3:1 (slika 1). Premik vode je odvisen od osmolarnosti kompartmentov, torej glede na koncentracijo elektrolitov v posameznem kompartmentu. Izmed elektrolitov je najpomembenjši Na+, ki ga zaužijemo predvsem v obliki soli. Vodo izgublja človek skozi kožo z znojenjem in z difuzijo, z urinom, iz prebavil z bruhanjem in blatom ter skozi dihala z difuzijo. Pri zdravi osebi je bilanca vode in natrija ničelna. Torej sta v ravnovesju. Glavni organ, ki vzdržuje ničelno bilanco so ledvice. Za zadosten vnos vode je glavni dražljaj žeja, pri izločanju vode pa sodelujejo številni fiziološki mehanizmi (sistem renin-angitenzin-aldosteron, natriuretični hormon, simpatična oživčenost ledvičnih arteriol in urodilantin). V tem članku bomo tako preleteli osnovne mehanizme vodnega in elektrolitskega ravnotežja in se osredotočili, kako se slednje spremeni med športom in kakšen je odziv telesa ob športnem naporu glede na vsebnost vode v telesu.
Slika 1. Porazdelitev vode v glavnih kompartmentih človeškega telesa.
2. HIPERHIDRACIJA
Hiperhidracija je stanje povečane vode v telesu, ki je posledica pozitivne bilance vode in Na+. Nastane zaradi povečanega vnosa in/ali zmanjšanega izločanja vode in soli (Na+) preko ledvic. Skupna značilnost vseh stanj hiperhidracije je povečan volumen ZUCP, na račun vode. Celokupna količina Na+ v ZUCP pa je ob tem lahko povečana ali normalna.
Poznamo 3 tipe hiperhidracije glede na prerazporeditev topljenca ( soli):
- Izotonična hiperhidracija: je posledica pozitivne bilance vode in soli. Vzroki za takšno stanje so lahko prevelik vnos izotonične tekočine pri zdravi osebi ali prevelik vnos vode in soli pri bolnikih s kronično ledvično boleznijo, kjer so ledvica preveč okvarjena, da bi lahko popravila takšno stanje.
- Hipertonična hiperhidracija: je posledica pozitivne bilance vode in soli, kjer je večji vnos soli, kot je vnos vode. Kaže se z zvišano koncentracijo Na+ v plazmi in povišano količino vode v ZUCP. Vzrok so lahko predoziranje s kortikosteroidi, zastrupitev z Na+ in razne klinične bolezni (Connov sindrom, Cushingov sindrom,..).
- Hipotonična hiperhidracija: je posledica pozitivne bilance vode in soli, kjer je koncentracija soli nižja kot je volumen vode. Koncentracija Na+ je nižja v plazmi, povečan pa je volumen ZUCP na račun vode. Klinične bolezni, ki povzročajo takšno stanje so kronično popuščanje srca, kronične bolezni jeter in nefrotski sindrom.
3. DEHIDRACIJA
Dehidracija je stanje, kjer pride do pomankanja vode v telesu in je posledica negativne bilance vode in soli. Govorimo o »izsušitvi«, kjer je izguba večja od vnosa. Takšno telesno stanje lahko vodi v hipovolemijo – padec telesnega tlaka v žilah, ki lahko povroži motnjo zavesti, splošno oslabelost, nemoč,.. Pri tem se aktivirajo mehanizmi za popravo in vzdrževanje tega stanja, kar ljudje občutijo kot izrazit nenaden občutek žeje, oligurijo – minimalno izločanje urina, tahikardijo – pospešeno bitje srca in akuten padec telesne teže.
Pri dehidraciji gre prav tako za 3 patofiziološke principe nastanka:
- Izotonična dehidracija: je posledica negativne bilance vode in soli, pri čemer je izguba v enakem razmerju. Klinična stanja, ki vodijo v to so driska, akutna zunanja krvavitev in akutna odpoved ledvic.
- Hipertonična dehidracija: je posledica negativne bilance vode in soli, kjer je izguba vode večja, kot je izguba soli. V tem primeru človek izgublja vodo iz ZUCP in ZNCP, ter sol iz ZUCP. Stanje, ki vodi v to je obilno potenje predvsem med športno aktivnostjo, kjer ne nadomeščamo izgubljene vode in soli. Lahko gre tudi za stanje nezmožnosti pitja vode, v primeru: nezavesti, duševne prizadetosti, pri otrocih ali dojenčkih.
- Hipotonična dehidracija: je posledica negativne bilance vode in soli, kjer gre za večjo izgubo soli, kot izgubo vode. Človek izgublja vodo iz ZUCP v seč. Tako je zmanjšan volumen krvi zaradi izgube vode. Takšno stanje lahko nastopi v primeru, ko športnik nadomešča izgubljeno tekočino samo z vodo, brez elektrolitov (brez soli) ali pri bolnikih z Addisonovo boleznijo (ki nimajo hormona aldosterona in kortizola).
4. HIPONATRIEMIJA IN ZASTRUPITEV Z VODO PRI ŠPORTU
Hiponatriemija opisuje stanje nižje koncentracije Na+ v krvi kot je normalno (135 - 145 mmol/l) in je najpogostejša elektrolitska motnja, ki ob hiperhidraciji lahko vodi v zastrupitev telesa z vodo. Kot smo že zgoraj omenili je Na+ ključen elektrolit in je tisti dejavnik, ki prepreči vodi, da bi vdrla v celice. V primeru hiponatriemije se zgodi, da voda vdre v celice in te nabreknejo. Ključen hormon odgovoren za uravnavanje ravnovesja vode v telesu je hormon AVP . Izloča se iz možganov - iz hipotalamusa, na stimulus zmanjšanega volumna v ZUCP. Do motenega izločanja iz hipotalamusa lahko pride zaradi nevropsihiatričnih motenj, infekcij, poškodb in krvavitev iz možganov. Zelo pogosti vzroki za takšno stanje so tudi zdravila, ki povzročajo hiponatriemijo po različnih mehanizmih.
V športni panogi se z njo srečamo zaradi prekomernega pitja hipotonične tekočine ob hudem telesnem naporu (kot je maraton). Imenujemo jo hiponatriemija zaradi telesnega napora (HZTN). Gre za akutno stanje z znižanjem koncentracije natrijevega iona v krvi pod 135 mmol/l. Rizični dejavniki za nastanek so nizka telesna masa, slabša treniranost, tek daljši od štirih ur, visoke okoljne temperature in pogosto pitje tekočine med tekom.
4.1. Mehanizem nastanka hiponatriemije zaradi telesnega napora
Primarni mehanizem HZTN je čezmerni vnos hipotonične tekočine kot so voda in razne športne pijače, v kombinaciji z zmanjšano sekrecijo vode v distalnem tubulu ledvic zaradi sproščanja hormona arginin vazopresina (AVP). To vidimo predvsem pri počasnejših maratoncih.
Hormon AVP je običajno ob nižji plazemski koncentraciji soli zavrt. Pri nekaterih atletih se to ne zgodi, kar lahko opazimo z neprimerno visoko osmolalnostjo seča – zelo koncentriran seč. Stimulusi za izločanje AVP so lahko bolečina, čustva, fizični napor, slabost, bruhanje, hipoglikemija, izpostavitev vročini, nesteroidni antirevmatiki,..
Izguba natrija z znojem se med posamezniki zelo razlikuje. Povečano potenje lahko vodi v nastanek hiponatremije zaradi izgube soli, povečanega izločanja AVP in vnosa tekočin, ki so bolj hipotonična kot pa znoj. Velika količina osmotsko neaktivnega natrija v telesu se nahaja v kosteh, koži in hrustancu ter se potencialno lahko pretvori v osmotsko aktivno obliko. HZTN bi lahko bila posledica nezmožnosti pretvorbe natrija v aktivno obliko.
4.2. Simptomi med telesnim naporom
Ob padcu koncentracije natrija v krvi sledi premik vode v celice. Simptomatska hiponatriemija se najpogosteje pokaže z nevrološko disfunkcijo. Najbolj so prizadeti možgani, ki se ne morejo širiti zaradi omejenosti prostora v lobanji. Ob tem se zveča intrakranialni tlak in zmanjša prekrvavitev možganov, kar se sprva kaže z glavobolom, prizadeto koordinacijo športnika, nastopi slabost in bruhanjem ter mišični krči. Nastopi zmedenost in okrnjena zavest. Kasneje se pojavi koma in zastoj dihanja zaradi utesnitve možganskega debla.
Ker so znaki hiponatriemije podobni tistim, ki nastanejo pri dehidraciji, je pomembno, da ocenimo stopnjo hidracije, ki jo pri športnikih bolje prikaže določanje osmolalnosti (koncentriranosti) seča in njegove specifične teže kot pa določanje osmolalnosti krvi. V praksi se uporablja kopalniški test, kjer se med vadbo meri akutno izgubo telesne mase zaradi izgube telesnih tekočin.
5. PRIPOROČILA VNOSA VODE IN ELEKTROLITOV MED VADBO
Pitje razredčenih glukozno elektrolitih raztopin je učinkovit način preprečevanja dehidracije in ugodno vpliva na telesno zmogljivost. Potrebe po vodi in elektrolitih so ob telesnem naporu odvisne od posameznika, okolja, intenzivnosti in trajanja napora. Športnik mora biti pred začetkom vadbe dobro hidriran z normalnimi vrednostmi elektrolitov v plazmi. Pitje tekočine med vadbo mora ustrezati izgubam tekočine s potenjem in uriniranjem. Med vadbo mora športnik zmanjševati dehidracijo tako, da izguba telesne teže ni večja od 2%. Za optimalno rehidracijo je potrebno popiti 1,5 litra tekočine za vsak izgubljen kilogram telesne mase. Športnik naj pije počasi, v majhnih količinah, vsakih 15 minut. Pijača naj vsebuje od 5 do 10 odstotkov ogljikovih hidratov, od 20 do 30 mmol/l natrija in od 2 do 5 mmol/l kalija. Dodatek natrija je priporočljiv pri vadbah, ki trajajo dlje kot 2 uri ali pri vadbah, kjer so izgube natrija z znojem visoke.
6. ZAKLJUČEK
Homeostatsko ravnovesje tekočin v telesu je pomembno za zdravo delovanje organizma. Vsaka celica v našem telesu za delovanje potrebuje vodo, ki ima med drugimi pomembno vlogo pri uravnavanju telesne temperature, transportu hranljivih snovi in odstranjevanju odpadnih produktov. Količina vode, ki jo je potrebno vnesti v telo je odvisna od klimatskih razmer in telesne aktivnost. Pomembna je športna ozaveščenost o primerni uporabi elektrolitskih napitkov v kombinaciji z vodo. Potrebna je prilagoditev glede na intenzivnost športne aktivnosti, glede na telesno vzdržljivost in konstitucijo ter povrniti telesu vse izgubljene snovi.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Elevated blood pressure and certain chronic kidney diseases can lead to complete kidney failure. In such cases, the blood must be cleansed using artificial kidneys (hemodialysis) or peritoneal dialysis; otherwise, the patient will die within a very short time due to body poisoning (uremia). Another treatment option for patients with end-stage renal disease is kidney transplantation.

The link between high blood pressure and kidney disease has been known for a long time. Prolonged high blood pressure can damage the kidneys, and chronic kidney diseases often cause high blood pressure, which further impairs kidney function and significantly contributes to the development of cardiovascular diseases, which are the leading cause of death in patients with chronic kidney disease.

The most common causes of chronic kidney disease are diabetes, untreated or inadequately treated arterial hypertension, and glomerulonephritis (a group of kidney diseases in which the glomeruli are primarily affected).

KIDNEY FUNCTION
The kidneys are paired organs located below the ribs. Each is bean-shaped, typically 12 cm long and 6 cm wide in adults, and weighs between 120 and 170 g. They are well-vascularized and maintain a stable fluid and electrolyte balance in the body. The basic structural and functional unit is the nephron, of which there are 800,000 to 1,200,000 in each kidney. A nephron consists of a glomerulus and a tubule. The glomerulus is made up of thin blood vessels (capillaries) with numerous pores that act as filters. Blood flows through the capillaries, carrying harmful substances produced during protein metabolism. These substances are excreted through the pores, which act as a filter. Urine flows through the tubules, from which electrolytes, proteins, and fluid are reabsorbed into the body in appropriate amounts. The tubules end in papillae, which have an opening through which urine flows into the renal pelvis, from which it flows into the ureter. Urine then flows through the ureter into the bladder.

The kidneys remove harmful substances produced during protein metabolism and regulate the appropriate fluid balance in the body. Every day, 180 liters of plasma are filtered in the kidneys, and 1.5 to 2 liters of urine are excreted.

The kidneys also produce important hormones: renin, which regulates blood pressure; erythropoietin, which stimulates the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow; and the active form of vitamin D, which maintains adequate calcium levels.

The most important warning signs of kidney disease
The most important warning signs of kidney disease are swelling around the eyes, face, and lower extremities, brownish or bloody urine, frequent urination, especially at night, or decreased urination that is not proportional to fluid intake, a burning or irritating sensation or pain during urination, high blood pressure, and lower back pain that is not related to physical activity.

Diagnosis of kidney disease
The oldest, simplest, and most important test is a urine analysis under a microscope. In the urine, an excessive number of red blood cells and proteins indicate kidney damage. Increased protein excretion in the urine indicates more severe kidney damage, and kidney function deteriorates more rapidly.

To assess kidney function, we measure the concentration of serum creatinine. An elevated concentration may indicate serious chronic kidney disease. If an elevated concentration of creatinine is found in the urine, this means that kidney function is reduced by more than half. We can more accurately measure kidney function by collecting a 24-hour urine sample (the patient receives written instructions and a container to collect the urine), determining the concentration of creatinine in the serum, and measuring the amount excreted in the urine. Based on the data obtained, we calculate the creatinine clearance.

However, a precise diagnosis of kidney disease requires numerous special tests, which patients undergo with a nephrologist.

Ultrasound of the urinary tract is used to assess the position and size of the kidneys, changes in kidney tissue, possible dilation of the collecting system, and the presence of cysts, tumors, or kidney stones. A special method is used to measure blood flow in the renal artery, which can identify possible narrowing of the renal arteries, which can also be a cause of high blood pressure, especially in older people with signs of atherosclerotic involvement of other organs. These are patients with angina pectoris and signs of atherosclerosis of the peripheral vessels, which manifests as pain in the legs after walking a short distance.

For the diagnosis of chronic kidney disease, which primarily affects the glomeruli (glomerulonephritis), the most important test is a kidney biopsy. In this test, the position of the kidney is determined using ultrasound, and then a small piece of kidney tissue is taken with a special needle and processed with special methods and examined under a light and electron microscope.

HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE
High blood pressure in patients with kidney disease often does not cause specific symptoms, but the consequences are severe and often become apparent only in the advanced stages of kidney disease.

The risk of heart and brain damage, which manifests as a heart attack, impaired heart function, or stroke, is even greater in patients with high blood pressure and impaired kidney function than in patients with high blood pressure and normal kidney function. Even slightly impaired kidney function significantly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.

Therefore, it is very important for patients with kidney disease to recognize the dangers of untreated or inadequately treated high blood pressure early on.

Treatment of high blood pressure
Treating high blood pressure prevents kidney disease caused by high blood pressure (hypertensive nephrosclerosis), improves kidney function in chronic kidney disease, and reduces the risk of death from cardiovascular disease. This can only be achieved with intensive and persistent treatment. Studies in many patients with chronic kidney disease have identified the blood pressure value that protects the kidneys, meaning that it stops or slows the progression of kidney disease. This is the blood pressure value that we aim to achieve with treatment, and it is called the target blood pressure.

The target blood pressure in the treatment of patients with high blood pressure and normal kidney function is 130/85 mm Hg or less.

The target blood pressure in patients with impaired kidney function is even lower and depends on the degree of impairment: in chronic kidney disease with less protein loss in the urine, it is 130/80 mm Hg or less; in chronic kidney disease with more protein loss in the urine, it is 125/75 mm Hg or less. In the treatment of arterial hypertension, even in chronic kidney disease, non-pharmacological measures are the first line of treatment.

NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL MEASURES
Eat a healthy diet, with plenty of vegetables and fruits, little meat, and use olive oil instead of animal fats, and moderately limit protein intake. Reducing salt intake (5-8 g per day) is an integral part of the "kidney diet." Salt retains water in the body, which can cause swelling and raise blood pressure, requiring more medication to control it. Drink enough to produce 1.5 to 2 liters of urine per day. Consult your doctor about the amount of fluid you need daily, as fluid intake may need to be limited in some diseases, such as kidney, liver, or heart disease.

Smoking worsens kidney disease, especially in diabetic patients, damages blood vessels throughout the body, and accelerates aging and atherosclerotic processes. High blood pressure due to narrowing of the renal artery, a consequence of atherosclerosis, is more than ten times more common in smokers than in non-smokers! It is also important to limit the use of pain relievers, as some can damage the kidneys or worsen the effects of medications that lower blood pressure, making blood pressure treatment ineffective.

Drug treatment
All medications that lower blood pressure can prevent kidney damage caused by hypertension and reduce protein loss in the urine. We use a special type of medication to lower blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease, which lowers blood pressure and further reduces protein loss in the urine.

These medications inhibit the renin-angiotensin system, a special system that affects the development and consequences of high blood pressure on the kidneys and heart. The effects of this system at different sites are inhibited by angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). High blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease is more difficult to treat than in patients without kidney disease. To achieve the target blood pressure, it is often necessary to combine at least two, often three or more medications. For effective and safe treatment, it is important to be aware of possible adverse drug interactions, and in patients with impaired kidney function, the dosage of medications must be adjusted to the degree of kidney impairment. Reduced protein loss in the urine indicates successful treatment of kidney disease, which can slow the progression of kidney disease or prevent complete kidney failure. Good cooperation between the patient and the doctor is especially important in patients with chronic kidney disease and is always a key factor in successful treatment, as treatment with many medications is often necessary for life.

Clinical Department of Nephrology,
University Medical Centre Ljubljana

Zvišan krvni tlak in nekatere kronične ledvične bolezni lahko povzročijo popolno ledvično odpoved. Takrat je treba čistiti kri z umetno ledvico (hemodializo) ali trebušno dializo (peritonealno dializo) sicer bolnik zaradi zastrupitve telesa (uremije) v zelo kratkem času umre. Druga možnost zdravljenja bolnikov s končno odpovedjo ledvic je presaditev ledvice (transplantacija).
Povezavo med zvišanim krvnim tlakom in boleznijo ledvic poznamo že dolgo. Dolgotrajno zvišan krvni tlak lahko okvari ledvice, kronične ledvične bolezni pa pogosto povzročijo zvišan krvni tlak, ki še poslabša delovanje ledvic in odločilno vpliva na nastanek srčno-žilnih bolezni, ki so na prvem mestu med vzroki smrti pri bolnikih s kronično ledvično boleznijo.
Najpogostejši vzroki kronične ledvične bolezni so sladkorna bolezen, nezdravljena ali neustrezno zdravljena arterijska hipertenzija in glomerulonefritisi (skupina ledvičnih bolezni, pri katerih so okvarjena predvsem ledvična telesca).
DELOVANJE LEDVIC
Ledvice so parni organ, leže pod rebri. Vsaka je fižolaste oblike, pri odraslem je običajno dolga 12 cm, široka 6 cm, tehta od 120 do 170 g. Dobro so prekrvljene in vzdržujejo stabilno tekočinsko in elektrolitsko ravnovesje v telesu.. Osnovna strukturna in funkcijska enota je nefron, v vsaki ledvici jih je od 800000 do 1200000. Nefron je sestavljen iz ledvičnega telesca (glomerula) in kanalčka (tubula). Glomerul je iz tankih krvnih žilic (kapilar), v katerih so številne luknjice, ki delujejo kot cedilca. Skozi kapilare teče kri, v kateri so škodljive snovi, nastale pri presnovi beljakovin. Te snovi se izločijo skozi luknjice, ki delujejo kot filter. Seč teče po tubulih, iz katerih se v telo vsrkajo elektroliti, beljakovine in tekočina za v telo ustrezni količini. Tubuli se končujejo v papilah, ki imajo odprtinico, skozi katero se seč izliva v ledvično čašico, iz nje v sečni meh, iz tega pa izhaja sečevod. Po sečevodu teče seč v sečni mehur.
Ledvice iz telesa odstranjujejo škodljive snovi, ki nastanejo pri presnovi beljakovin in uravnavajo ustrezno ravnovesje tekočin v telesu. Vsak dan se v ledvicah prečisti 180 litrov plazme, in izloči od 1,5 do 2 litra seča.
V ledvicah nastajajo tudi pomembni hormoni: renin, ki uravnava krvni tlak, eritropoetin, ki pospešuje nastajanje rdečih krvnih telesc v kostnem mozgu, in aktivna oblika vitamina D, ki vzdržuje ustrezne količine kalcija.
Najpomembnejši opozorilni znaki ledvičnih bolezni
Najpomembnejši opozorilni znaki ledvičnih bolezni so otekanje okolice oči, obraza in spodnjih udov, rjavkast ali krvav seč, pogosto uriniranje, predvsem ponoči, ali zmanjšano uriniranje, ki ni v sorazmerju s popito tekočino, pekoč, dražeč občutek ali bolečina med uriniranjem, zvišan krvni tlak in ledvena bolečina, ki ni povezana s telesno dejavnostjo.
Ugotavljanje ledvične bolezeni
Najstarejša, najpreprostejša in najpomembnejša preiskava je pregled seča pod mikroskopom. V seču opozarja na ledvično okvaro čezmerno število eritrocitov in beljakovin. Večje izločanje beljakovin s sečem pomeni hujšo ledvično okvaro, in ledvično delovanje se hitreje slabša.
Za oceno ledvičnega delovanja izmerimo koncentracijo serumskega kreatinina. Zvišana koncentracija je lahko znak resne kronične ledvične bolezeni. Kadar ugotovimo v seču zvišano koncentracijo kreatinina, to pomeni, da je ledvično delovanje zmanjšano za več kot polovico. Natančneje izmerimo ledvično delovanje z zbiranjem 24-urnega seča ( bolnik dobi pisna navodila in posodo, v katero zbira seč), določitvijo koncentracije kreatinina v serumu in izločene količine v seču. Na podlagi dobljenih podatkov izračunamo očistek kreatinina.
Za natančno diagnozo ledvične bolezni pa so potrebne še številne posebne preiskave, ki jih bolniki opravijo pri specialistu nefrologu.
Z ultrazvokom sečil ocenjujemo položaj in velikost ledvic, spremembe ledvičnega tkiva, morebitno razširitev votlega sistema, pojav cist, tumorjev ali ledvičnih kamnov. S posebno metodo merimo pretok krvi v ledvični arteriji in tako ugotavljamo morebitne zožitve ledvičnih arterij, tudi to je lahko vzrok za zvišan krvni tlak, predvsem pri starejših ljudeh z znaki aterosklerotične prizadetosti drugih organov. To so bolniki z angino pektoris in znaki ateroskleroze perifernih žil, ki se kaže z bolečinami v nogah že po krajši hoji.
Za diagnozo kronične ledvične bolezni, ki je prizadela predvsem ledvična telesca (glomerulonefritisi) je najpomembnejša preiskava ledvična biopsija. Pri tej preiskavi s pomočjo ultrazvoka določijo položaj ledvice, nato pa s posebno iglo odvzamejo košček ledvičnega tkiva, da ga s posebnimi metodami obdelajo in natančno pregledajo s svetlobnim in z elektronskim mikroskopom.
ZVIŠAN KRVNI TLAK
Zvišan krvni tlak tudi pri bolnikih z ledvično boleznijo pogosto ne povzroča posebnih bolezenskih znamenj, vendar pa so posledice hude, pogosto očitne šele v napredovalem stadiju ledvične bolezni.

Ciljni krvni tlak pri bolnikih z oslabelim ledvičnim delovanjem je še nižji in je odvisen od stopnje okvare: pri kronični ledvični bolezni z manjšim izgubljanjem beljakovin s sečem je 130/80 mm Hg ali manj. pri kronični ledvični bolezni z večjim izgubljanjem beljakovin s sečem je 125/75 mm Hg ali manj. Interesting Facts
Organisms depend on their environment
When we go into the field, we are interested not only in the organisms but also in the environment in which they live. Therefore, we always first observe the general characteristics of the water body, such as depth, water level, shading, and the type of sediment, as well as the stabilization of the bank, vegetation, and the width of the riparian zone, and the use of land in the hinterland. All of this affects the organisms that live there. Then we measure the temperature, pH, conductivity, oxygen concentration, and water transparency. If we are interested in more details, we can also measure the concentration of nutrients (e.g., nitrogen or phosphorus), sodium, calcium, potassium, and the like in the laboratory.
Temperature, pH, conductivity, and oxygen concentration in the water are measured with a multimeter with various sensors.
- Temperature affects many processes in the water; at higher temperatures, gases are less soluble, the decomposition of organic matter occurs faster, and cyanobacteria and algae grow faster, so the likelihood of cyanobacterial blooms is greater.
- pH indicates the acidity or alkalinity of the water. This affects the availability of nutrients in the water and the solubility of some minerals, such as heavy metals. The pH changes depending on various natural factors (e.g., rocks and soil, precipitation, vegetation), but it can also reflect pollution (e.g., acid rain, mining, wastewater, chemicals from agriculture). High concentrations of cyanobacteria and algae raise the pH of the water because they consume a lot of carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
- Conductivity is the ability of water to conduct electric current; it tells us how many ions (salts) are dissolved in the water. Salts come from rocks that the water breaks down and carries with it, so conductivity depends on the type of rock and soil. Conductivity is higher in drier periods because dissolved substances are concentrated in a smaller amount of water, and at higher temperatures. In addition, various pollutants in the water can increase its conductivity, so a sudden increase in conductivity is a good indicator of pollution.
- Oxygen concentration depends on the speed of the water flow, temperature, and salinity, but the amount of algae and cyanobacteria that produce oxygen, and the amount of organic matter that is broken down by bacteria and consumes oxygen, are also key.
We measure the transparency or turbidity of the water with a Secchi disk – a white plate on a rope with markings for individual lengths, which we immerse in the water and measure the depth at which the plate appears to disappear. This is called the Secchi depth; the smaller the Secchi depth, the greater the turbidity of the water.
The Secchi depth tells us how many particles are in the water – these can be non-living (various sediments, e.g., sand or clay) or living (algae, cyanobacteria). Some of these particles can have a negative impact on the ecosystem because they inhibit the flow of light, suffocate aquatic animals, or carry pollutants and pathogenic organisms. With the help of the Secchi depth, we also estimate the depth to which light still reaches – this is the area where algae and cyanobacteria can survive. In this way, we determine the sampling depth in deep lakes, such as Lake Bled and Lake Bohinj.
In addition, we can sometimes measure the concentration of nutrients (e.g., nitrogen or phosphorus) in the laboratory. Nutrients can come from fertilizers from agricultural land, sewage, or other wastewater. Their elevated concentrations promote the excessive growth of cyanobacteria and algae.

What is rubella?
Rubella is an infection caused by the rubella virus. The symptoms of the infection are usually mild, but if it occurs during pregnancy, it can cause serious harm to the unborn child, including deafness. Rubella can be prevented – since 1969, vaccination programs have led to a dramatic decrease in the incidence of rubella virus infection. Let's look at some facts about rubella:
- Rubella is a viral infection that is often spread through coughing,
- the virus can pass through the placenta and affect the fetus,
- in about ½ of cases, the symptoms are so mild that many people don't even notice them,
- rubella can cause deafness in the unborn child,
- vaccination is the only way to prevent infection.
Symptoms (how to recognize them):
The rash in rubella infection is a mild pink color and is lighter than the rash that accompanies measles. Rubella is also called German measles. Symptoms appear about 14–21 days after infection.
The rash first appears on the face and then spreads to the neck and limbs. After about 3–5 days, the rash fades and eventually disappears. It can be itchy. Other symptoms include:
- Stuffy or runny nose,
- headache,
- fever,
- red and inflamed eyes,
- inflammation of the nerves,
- swollen lymph nodes,
- joint pain.
Infection can occur at any age, but it rarely affects infants and people over 40. A person who is infected after the age of 40 usually has more severe symptoms than a child.
Treatment:
There is no medicine to shorten a rubella infection, but symptoms can be relieved – when they are mild, treatment is practically not necessary. A person infected with rubella should avoid contact with pregnant women and anyone with a weakened immune system – avoidance is necessary for up to 1 week after the symptoms of the infection have ended.
If a child has rubella, the school they attend should also be informed.
Plants as a natural aid:
- Aloe vera can be used whenever rashes or inflammation appear on our skin. The gel has a very pleasant, cooling effect that relieves itching and soothes inflammation. The gel can also be used to care for the skin in rubella infection.
- Calendula has been known for many years as a plant that relieves inflammation. Instead of calendula oil for skin care, choose calendula cream, which is absorbed more quickly into the skin and does not leave a greasy feeling on its surface.
- Lavender soothes the skin, and its pleasant scent relaxes the body and mind. Lavender oil can be mixed with calendula ointment, as both have antimicrobial properties. They are an excellent natural solution for any skin rashes.
Prevention:
The best way to prevent infection is to get vaccinated against the rubella virus, but we can also do a lot by avoiding people we know are infected with rubella. Vaccination is also recommended before traveling, as the virus is much more widespread in some countries than it is here. If you are planning a pregnancy, make sure you are 100% protected against rubella infection.

The basic vaccination against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, and Haemophilus influenzae type b consists of three doses of the vaccine. To boost and extend immunity, a booster vaccination is required one year after the third dose.
Children are vaccinated in their first year of life, receiving the first dose at three months, the second dose at four to five months, and the third dose at six months. The fourth dose is given between 12 and 24 months of age.

The basic vaccination against measles, mumps, and rubella consists of two doses of the vaccine. The first dose is given after the child reaches 12 to 18 months of age, and the second dose is given before starting school.
The hepatitis B vaccination consists of three doses of the vaccine. The first dose is given before starting school, and the other two doses are given after starting school.
Diphtheria
Diphtheria is a serious disease that begins with a sore throat and progresses to difficulty breathing. The bacteria can damage the heart and nervous system, and severe forms of the disease can be life-threatening. The last case of diphtheria in our country was recorded in 1967.
Tetanus
Tetanus is a disease that affects the nervous system and can lead to severe muscle spasms. These can cause breathing difficulties and be life-threatening. The disease is caused by the tetanus bacillus, which is found in the soil and can enter the body through wounds, punctures, burns, and the like.

Pertussis is a disease that causes severe coughing fits and breathing difficulties. The disease can last for up to 10 weeks. It is most dangerous for children under one year of age and can cause severe brain damage and be life-threatening. In older children, the disease occurs in a milder form. Before the introduction of mandatory pertussis vaccination, about seven thousand children were affected annually in our country.
Polio
Polio is caused by a virus that attacks the nervous system and causes permanent paralysis of the muscles. Before polio vaccination was introduced in our country, about 250 children were affected annually.

Infection with this bacterium can cause several serious forms of the disease, the most common being meningitis. The vaccine protects the child against meningitis caused by this bacterium, but not against other types of meningitis. Complications, such as pneumonia, febrile seizures, and encephalitis, cannot be predicted in advance, but they affect one in every 15 children. In severe cases, it can be life-threatening.

The infection is most dangerous in the first three months of pregnancy and can cause damage to the vision, hearing, heart, and brain of the fetus.
Hepatitis B
Hepatitis B is a viral liver disease that can affect people of any age. If infants and young children become infected, they are more likely to become carriers of the virus. The virus is present in the body fluids of an infected person, so there is a high risk that children whose mothers are infected will become infected with the disease during pregnancy or childbirth.
Mumps
Mumps spreads in the same way as measles and is highly contagious. Infection with the mumps virus can cause a high fever, headache, and swelling of the parotid and other glands.
